https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362545.headline: Abbeyfeale Homeowners Targeted as Thieves Siphon Heating Oil From Vacant Property
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362545.summary: Gardaí in Abbeyfeale have launched an investigation after thieves siphoned home heating oil from a property left vacant for two weeks. Authorities have issued a security warning to homeowners across Limerick as colder weather arrives.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362545.story:
Gardaí in Abbeyfeale are investigating the theft of home heating oil from a local property after thieves targeted a house that had been vacant for just two weeks. When the homeowners returned to the premises, they discovered that the oil had been siphoned directly from their tank.

In response to the incident, Crime Prevention Officer Sergeant Michelle O’Halloran has issued a timely warning to residents across Limerick as temperatures begin to drop. She urged homeowners to ensure their oil tanks are properly secured ahead of the winter months.

"If possible, consider installing a lockable tank cover or security cage, and make sure the tank is positioned in a secure and well-lit area," Sergeant O’Halloran said. She added that external lighting, CCTV systems, and house alarms can also serve as effective deterrents against fuel theft.

Authorities have also advised residents who plan on leaving their homes vacant for any period of time to ask a trusted neighbour to keep a watchful eye on the property and immediately report any suspicious activity to local Gardaí.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362545.localAngle: The incident occurred at a property in Abbeyfeale, prompting local Gardaí to issue a winter security warning for homeowners across Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362545.originalTitle: Limerick Gardaí warn of theft of home heating oil as colder months set in

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53246.headline: Limerick Dementia Social Club Announces Autumn and Winter Programme of Activities
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53246.summary: The Limerick Dementia Social Club has released its upcoming schedule of events at Our Lady of Lourdes Community Centre on Childers Road, offering music, choirs, and support sessions for people living with dementia and their carers.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53246.story:
The Limerick Dementia Social Club has announced its new schedule of activities for the coming months, offering a regular meeting space for people living with dementia and their carers on the first Wednesday of every month.

Held at Our Lady of Lourdes Community Centre on Childers Road from 6.30pm to 8.45pm, the club aims to provide a non-judgemental space to socialise and combat isolation. Established in 2018 by Mags O’Sullivan and her co-workers, the initiative connects members with local performers, including a planned ‘Fleming Ball’ and a ‘Craic agus Ceol’ session on Wednesday, November 4. Professional music therapist Cathy McGlynn also leads the ‘Melodies Memory Choir’ every third Wednesday.

Ms O’Sullivan noted the profound impact of music on attendees, particularly those experiencing communication difficulties. "We have people in the club that have difficulty with communication and expressive language, yet when we sing together, they may remember a whole verse of a song," she said. In addition to music, monthly gatherings feature guest speakers providing practical advice on nutrition, mobility, and care strategies for carers.

The club will host a Christmas Festive Evening and fundraiser with a raffle and spot prizes on Wednesday, December 2. Anyone seeking further information on the upcoming schedule can contact Mags O’Sullivan via email at limerickdementiasc@gmail.com.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53246.localAngle: The club provides vital social and support services for dementia patients and their carers at Our Lady of Lourdes Community Centre on Childers Road.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53246.originalTitle: Music and community at the heart of Limerick Dementia Social Club this season

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362602.headline: Gardaí seize €644,000 of cocaine and heroin during Old Singland Road search
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362602.summary: Limerick Gardaí arrested a woman in her 40s after uncovering €490,000 of cocaine and €154,000 of heroin at a residential property on Wednesday.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362602.story:
Gardaí in Limerick have seized a significant quantity of illegal drugs with an estimated street value of €644,000 following a search on the city's east side.

Officers attached to the Limerick Divisional Drug Unit carried out the search under warrant at a residential property on Old Singland Road on Wednesday, October 28. During the operation, which formed part of an ongoing targeted campaign against drug distribution in the Mid-West region, officers uncovered €490,000 worth of cocaine alongside €154,000 of heroin.

A woman aged in her 40s was arrested at the scene in connection with the intelligence-led seizure. She is currently being held in Garda custody in the Limerick area under the provisions of Section 2 of the Criminal Justice Act 1996.

Gardaí have confirmed that the investigation remains ongoing as officers continue to target the supply of controlled substances across the region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362602.localAngle: The major drugs seizure took place at a residential property on Old Singland Road as part of an operation targeting criminal networks across the Mid-West.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362602.originalTitle: Cocaine and heroin valued €644,000 seized in Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362583.headline: Limerick Bus Drivers Targeted as Fireworks Thrown into Vehicles Ahead of Halloween
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362583.summary: Bus services in Limerick, including the 303 and Expressway Route 13, have faced temporary suspensions after gangs threw fireworks into vehicles, terrifying passengers and drivers.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362583.story:
Bus drivers operating in parts of Limerick are facing dangerous conditions in the run-up to Halloween, with gangs of youths throwing fireworks directly into vehicles. The disruption has forced the temporary suspension of certain services, predominantly impacting the 303 route between Pineview and Kilmallock Road, as well as Expressway Route 13 connecting Limerick and Tralee.

Aontú Councillor Sarah Beasley said drivers have contacted her at their wits' end. One driver reported that a firework exploded inside a bus, leaving an elderly passenger terrified. Cllr Beasley noted that drivers are naturally reluctant to enter certain estates after dark, resulting in significant inconvenience for regular public transport users who rely on the services.

Bus Éireann confirmed that services have experienced recent anti-social behaviour and will be curtailed wherever there is a risk to safety. Additional security has been arranged across Limerick for the Halloween period, and the company is liaising closely with An Garda Síochána. Officials have also reiterated that the possession, sale, or use of unlicensed fireworks is illegal, carrying penalties of up to €10,000 in fines and five years in prison.

The recent transport incidents follow an earlier occurrence this month on the 303 route, where child vandals concealed Stanley-type blades in bus seats, causing extensive damage to the upholstery and putting passengers at serious risk.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362583.localAngle: Public transport routes across Limerick City and surrounding areas are experiencing severe disruptions and safety hazards due to anti-social behaviour ahead of Halloween.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362583.originalTitle: Limerick bus drivers “terrorised” in run up to Halloween

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53250.headline: Limerick striker Ronan Coughlan helps Fleetwood Town knock Arsenal out of Carabao Cup
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53250.summary: Limerick-born Ronan Coughlan scored in a penalty shootout as League Two side Fleetwood Town pulled off a shock Carabao Cup win against Premier League champions Arsenal.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53250.story:
Limerick native Ronan Coughlan played a pivotal role on Tuesday night as Fleetwood Town pulled off a major upset, eliminating Premier League champions Arsenal from the Carabao Cup at Highbury Stadium.

The 30-year-old striker stepped up to score the first penalty in a 5-3 shootout victory after the match ended 1-1 following 120 minutes of play. Aaron Loupalo-Bi had opened the scoring for Fleetwood in the 21st minute before Viktor Gyökeres equalised for Arsenal. The Premier League side was reduced to ten players in the 85th minute when 16-year-old Max Dowman received a red card. Belfast-born teenager Conor Haughey scored the decisive penalty to secure the quarter-final spot for the League Two club.

Coughlan's football journey began locally with Mungret Regional before he progressed to Limerick FC and subsequently moved to English side Huddersfield Town. After spells with Bray Wanderers, Cork City, Sligo Rovers, St Patrick’s Athletic—where he won the 2021 FAI Cup—and Waterford, he joined Fleetwood Town in 2024.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53250.localAngle: Limerick-born striker Ronan Coughlan helped secure Fleetwood Town's shock Carabao Cup victory over Arsenal, bringing national attention back to his footballing roots in Mungret Regional.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53250.originalTitle: Limerick striker stars in shock Carabao Cup upset over Arsenal

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362551.headline: Students at Catherine McAuley School celebrate Halloween with fancy dress
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362551.summary: Students and staff at the Catherine McAuley School marked the mid-term season with a Halloween party featuring costumes and trick-or-treating.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362551.story:
Students and staff at the Catherine McAuley School recently marked the Halloween season with a festive school party filled with traditional celebrations.

The event featured a range of spooky costumes worn by students, alongside activities including trick-or-treating.

Photographs from the day captured the celebrations as the school community gathered to mark the occasion ahead of the mid-term break.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362551.localAngle: The event brought together students and staff at the local Limerick school for annual Halloween celebrations.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362551.originalTitle: IN PHOTOS: Catherine McAuley School Halloween party

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362612.headline: Limerick Libraries launch county-wide 'One Limerick, One Book' reading initiative
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362612.summary: Limerick Libraries and Creative Ireland have launched a new community reading initiative, selecting local author Karen Fitzgibbon's thriller 'Tell The Truth' as its inaugural title.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362612.story:
Bookworms across Limerick are being encouraged to read, discuss, and share the same novel under a newly launched county-wide reading initiative. 

'One Limerick, One Book' has been introduced by Limerick Libraries with support from the Creative Ireland Programme. Based on the successful 'One County, One Book' model, the scheme aims to connect communities throughout the city and county through a shared reading experience.

Thriller novel *Tell The Truth*, written by local author Karen Fitzgibbon, has been chosen as the very first title for the programme. Organisers based the selection on criteria including a strong local connection through the author, setting, or subject matter, broad appeal for general readers and book clubs, and sufficient availability of copies for a county-wide rollout.

Author Karen Fitzgibbon welcomed the announcement, describing her inclusion as a real honour. "A strong sense of place is incredibly important to me when I’m writing, and *Tell The Truth* is very much a Limerick story," she said.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362612.localAngle: The initiative connects readers across Limerick city and county through a shared reading experience featuring a local author and setting.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362612.originalTitle: New reading initiative launched in Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362608.headline: Rhebogue Mum Celebrates 18 Months Smoke-Free After QUIT Mid West Support
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362608.summary: Claire Crawford, 29, from Rhebogue has marked 18 months as a non-smoker after receiving support from QUIT Mid West during her fourth pregnancy at University Maternity Hospital Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362608.story:
A Limerick mother is celebrating nearly a year and a half free of cigarettes after getting support from the HSE’s QUIT Mid West service. 29-year-old Claire Crawford from Rhebogue had smoked since her teenage years and successfully kicked the habit after being referred through University Maternity Hospital Limerick (UMHL) during her fourth pregnancy.

Working with Stop Smoking Advisor Niamh Keating, Ms Crawford stopped smoking immediately upon referral and was completely nicotine-free within 20 weeks. She noted that previous attempts to quit during earlier pregnancies had failed because she could never last more than a few hours, but the regular advice and structure provided by the service made the crucial difference.

As well as health improvements, including better recovery after a caesarean section and the ability to breastfeed her youngest baby for the first time, Ms Crawford highlighted the financial impact. She previously spent around €150 a week on smoking, funds that are now redirected toward family activities and maintaining a smoke-free household for her children, coinciding with the national 'Stoptober' campaign.

Those looking for further information on quitting smoking can visit the HSE website at HSE.ie/QuitSmoking.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362608.localAngle: The story highlights a local mother from Rhebogue and her journey with the University Maternity Hospital Limerick-linked QUIT Mid West service.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362608.originalTitle: Limerick mum celebrates over one year smoke-free thanks to QUIT Mid West

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362605.headline: Council Warned Murdered Pensioner Over Illegal Tenant Living in Home
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362605.summary: The Central Criminal Court heard that Tipperary County Council flagged concerns to 89-year-old Josie Ray about an unauthorized occupant in her home months before she was allegedly murdered. The trial of Hasan Ali Gori, who has pleaded not guilty to the murder, is currently underway in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362605.story:
The Central Criminal Court heard this week that Tipperary County Council had contacted 89-year-old Josephine “Josie” Ray regarding concerns that a man was living illegally in her home prior to her alleged murder. Ms Ray, of St Joseph’s Park, Nenagh, was found strangled and smothered in her bed on August 4, 2024. The accused, 52-year-old Hasan Ali Gori, originally from Chad and with an address at St Joseph’s Park, has pleaded not guilty to the murder before Mr Justice Sean Gillane and a jury.

At the time of the alleged killing, Ali Gori was in a relationship with Ms Ray’s daughter, Mary Ray, who lived with an intellectual disability. Relatives and neighbours testified that the household was marked by constant arguments and fighting among the three residents. Seamus O’Brien, a community liaison officer with the council, gave evidence that he visited Ms Ray in April 2024 to inform her that, under her tenancy terms, no occupants other than her daughter were permitted in the property. A subsequent letter regarding anti-social behaviour and unauthorized occupancy was also sent to Ms Ray, warning that her tenancy was at risk.

Gardai told the court they responded to a domestic disturbance at the home on the night before Ms Ray was found dead. Garda Aoife Shine stated that Mary Ray was upset and claimed her partner was talking to prostitutes on his phone, while Ali Gori appeared frustrated. Another neighbour testified that he overheard the accused telling Mary Ray that either he had to go or Josie had to leave the house. The prosecution's case is that Ali Gori strangled and smothered the pensioner during the ongoing domestic friction.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362605.localAngle: The high-profile murder trial is taking place before the Central Criminal Court sitting in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362605.originalTitle: Council told murder victim that accused was illegal tenant

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362593.headline: Limerick family-run Santa’s Magical Cabin marks 17 years and 700,000th customer
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362593.summary: The Limerick-operated festive attraction is celebrating its 17th year with six nationwide locations in partnership with Dunnes Stores, on track to welcome its 700,000th customer this Christmas.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362593.story:
Santa’s Magical Cabin is marking its 17th year of operation, with the Limerick family-run business on track to welcome its 700,000th customer across its six nationwide locations this Christmas. 

Operating in partnership with Dunnes Stores, the nationally recognised festive event employs 100 local people at its Limerick base during the Christmas season. The attraction features professional photography and has built a strong reputation for inclusivity, catering specifically to families with children who have additional needs, disabilities, and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD).

As part of its ongoing charity efforts, the company has partnered with the Jack & Jill Foundation for the third consecutive year, gifting 130 family visits across its six sites to Jack & Jill families. The attraction also offers corporate packages with bespoke booking codes for employee visits.

Santa will officially arrive at the Jetland Shopping Centre on Sunday, November 15, with pre-arrival entertainment including face painters, balloon artists, and festive characters beginning at 12:30pm ahead of his arrival at 1:30pm.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362593.localAngle: The nationally successful festive attraction is proudly Limerick family-owned and operated, employing 100 local staff each Christmas season at the Jetland Shopping Centre.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362593.originalTitle: Santa’s Magical Cabin– Bringing Christmas Magic to Families for 17 Years

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362620.headline: Council reviews planning history and retail guidelines for Abbeyfeale's Sheehy site
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362620.summary: Limerick City and County Council is finalising a series of assessments regarding the Sheehy site in Abbeyfeale. The review includes examining a previous An Coimisiún Pleanála refusal and national retail planning guidelines.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362620.story:
Plans for the Sheehy site in Abbeyfeale have moved forward as Limerick City and County Council works to finalise a series of key assessments. Fine Gael councillor Liam Galvin was informed of the ongoing review following inquiries into the potential future of the West Limerick location.

According to Senior Council Planner Maria Woods, the local authority's current work involves reviewing the grounds behind a previous planning refusal from An Coimisiún Pleanála. Officials are also examining the relevant retail strategy context alongside the Department’s Retail Planning Guidelines as part of the process.

Ms Woods noted that any future proposal to rezone the Abbeyfeale property would require a substantial case to be made. “Should the Sheehy site be considered for rezoning, a robust planning argument and justification will be required to support any proposed change,” she stated.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362620.localAngle: The updates directly impact future development and planning strategy in the West Limerick town of Abbeyfeale.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362620.originalTitle: Update on plans for Sheehy site in Abbeyfeale

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362618.headline: Over 4,000 Prospective Students Attend TUS Moylish Campus Open Days
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362618.summary: More than 4,000 students from across the Mid West and beyond visited the Technological University of the Shannon in Limerick for the annual two-day open event.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362618.story:
More than 4,000 prospective students descended on the Technological University of the Shannon (TUS) Moylish campus for the university's annual two-day open event.

Held across Friday, October 15, and Saturday, October 16, the event welcomed visitors from the Mid West and further afield. Attendees were given the opportunity to explore the wide range of academic programmes available at the university and learn more about student life.

During the two-day event, prospective students had the chance to meet with current students and lecturers, as well as attend a packed schedule of course talks covering numerous disciplines. Visitors also engaged directly with representatives from Student Support, Access, Erasmus, and the Sports Office to gather information on campus resources and opportunities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362618.localAngle: The event drew thousands of visitors to Limerick's TUS Moylish campus to explore higher education opportunities in the region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362618.originalTitle: Thousands of prospective students visit Limerick for open days

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362633.headline: Former Milk Market takeaway transformed into training centre for adults with intellectual disabilities
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362633.summary: A disused takeaway unit at the Limerick Milk Market has been converted into a new training hub funded by The Michael Guinee Charitable Foundation. The Rising Together Training Centre will provide adults with intellectual disabilities pathways into employment through practical food and hospitality skills.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362633.story:
A disused takeaway unit at the heart of the Limerick Milk Market has been given a new lease of life as a fully equipped training facility for adults with intellectual disabilities. Funded by The Michael Guinee Charitable Foundation (MGCF), the new home of the Rising Together Training Centre (RTTC) aims to provide practical, vocational pathways into employment for its participants.

Open Monday to Friday, the centre offers training in baking, cooking, barista skills, catering, and hospitality. Alongside the educational programmes, the team will offer takeaway options including sandwiches, soups, treats, pizza slices, and pastries, as well as off-site catering services. 

David Fitzgerald, General Manager of the Limerick Milk Market, said the project delivers on a long-held ambition to establish a food training centre within Limerick's food community. Derek Barrett, Chief Executive of MGCF, noted that the project focuses on creating genuine opportunities for people with intellectual disabilities to participate more fully in employment and community life.

Laura Holland, Founder and CEO of Rising Together Training Programmes, highlighted the positive impact the initiative has had on participants' confidence and skill development. Meanwhile, Liam Flannery, Chairman of the Limerick Market Trustees, added that the centre will also benefit the wider local hospitality industry by supplying trained personnel ready to enter the workforce.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362633.localAngle: The initiative transforms a vacant unit inside the iconic Limerick Milk Market into an inclusive food training hub for the local community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362633.originalTitle: Former takeaway unit at Limerick Milk Market given new lease of life

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362631.headline: Prison watchdog slams single nurse on duty for 755 inmates when Limerick gang figure died
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362631.summary: A damning report reveals just one nurse was on duty at Mountjoy Prison to handle medical emergencies for 755 inmates on the night Limerick native David Stanners died in his cell in 2023.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362631.story:
A prison watchdog has branded it "unacceptable" that only a single nurse was on duty to provide emergency medical responses for 755 prisoners on the night well-known Limerick gangland figure David Stanners died in his cell.

Mr Stanners, 51, originally from Pineview Gardens in Moyross, was serving a life sentence for the 2003 murder of rival gang member Kieran Keane. According to a new report from the Office of the Inspector of Prisons (OIP), prison staff entered his cell just before midnight on October 25, 2023, after an officer noticed they could not see him in his bed. The sole nurse on duty attempted CPR before an Advanced Paramedic later pronounced him dead at 00:30am. A postmortem later concluded he died from ischemic cardiomyopathy, alongside severe coronary artery disease and recent consumption of cocaine.

During a Critical Incident Review Meeting, the nurse who attempted resuscitation described how difficult it was for one staff member to perform prolonged CPR, a sentiment backed by the Chief Nurse Officer. Despite the OIP repeatedly recommending that prison officers be trained in CPR, the service continues to refuse. The watchdog noted that while the prison population has since surged to well over 1,000, a follow-up inspection in 2025 found that staffing levels at night remained unchanged at just one nurse.

In addition to the staffing concerns, the OIP recommended that doctors conduct clinical reviews when nursing staff raise alarms over the repeated requests and potential overuse of prescription medication by specific prisoners. The report highlighted that prior to his death, a nurse had noted Mr Stanners attended every drug round requesting paracetamol and required a GP review.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362631.localAngle: David Stanners was a 51-year-old Limerick native from Moyross who was serving a life sentence for his involvement in the city's notorious gang feud.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362631.originalTitle: Only one prison nurse for 755 people on night Limerick man died

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362574.headline: Singer-songwriter Shirley Callaghan releases dark folk single exploring Ireland's institutional legacy
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362574.summary: Limerick-connected singer-songwriter Shirley Callaghan has released 'House of Love', a dark folk track reflecting on the treatment of women and children in Ireland's institutions.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362574.story:
Singer-songwriter Shirley Callaghan has released her new single, 'House of Love', a dark folk track that examines the treatment of women and children within Ireland’s institutional system and the lasting legacy of those facilities after their closure.

Known for atmospheric songwriting and emotive vocals, Callaghan says the song looks beyond the walls of those institutions to focus on the psychological and emotional scars carried by survivors and their families. Though first asked to write the track years ago, the artist struggled to find an approach until a collaborative writing session in Málaga with fellow musicians Paul and Sandra.

“This is a song I was first asked to write a number of years ago. The subject stayed with me, and I made many attempts over the years to find a way into the song,” Callaghan said. “When Paul, Sandra and I eventually came together for a writing session in Málaga, the song finally found its voice.”

“House of Love comes from a very difficult part of recent Irish history, but for many people its consequences are not simply history,” she added. “I wanted the song to reflect something of that experience and to honour stories that needed to be told.” The single is currently available to stream and support on Bandcamp.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362574.localAngle: The release comes from Limerick-connected singer-songwriter Shirley Callaghan, bringing local creative talent to a song exploring a significant chapter of Irish social history.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362574.originalTitle: Shirley Callaghan releases haunting new single ‘House of Love’ on the legacy of Ireland’s institutions

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362622.headline: Limerick Councillors Clash with Mayor Moran Over Proposed Crescent Road Closure
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362622.summary: Elected representatives at the Metropolitan District meeting criticized Mayor John Moran’s plans to close The Crescent for six weeks over the Christmas period, arguing it disrupts traffic and impacts local businesses during peak trading.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362622.story:
Limerick councillors have voiced strong opposition to Mayor John Moran’s plans to close The Crescent during the busy Christmas shopping period. During the latest Metropolitan District meeting, local representatives questioned the necessity of the six-week road closure, arguing it disrupts traffic on a main artery into the city.

Elected members raised concerns that the closure would negatively impact traders and businesses in what they described as a core commercial district. Councillors suggested alternative locations for festive markets and events, such as Bedford Row, Thomas Street, or Cruises Street, to avoid causing disruption to shoppers and local businesses during peak retail weeks.

Cllr Joe Leddin called on Mayor Moran to reconsider the move and show leadership, noting that the area functions primarily as a business district rather than a retail hub. Cllr Catherine Slattery also criticized the decision to block off the road, stating she is standing up for local voices affected by the traffic restrictions, while other members questioned the ongoing rationale behind the recurring closures.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362622.localAngle: The proposed road closure directly affects traffic flow, retail trade, and shoppers navigating Limerick city centre during the Christmas period.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362639.headline: MIC graduate Gearoid Mulvihill wins international award for Irish hip-hop research
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362639.summary: A Mary Immaculate College graduate has received international recognition at the Global Undergraduate Awards for his research exploring Irish hip-hop and traditional poetry.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362639.story:
A Mary Immaculate College (MIC) alumnus has earned international recognition for academic research exploring the connections between Irish hip-hop and traditional poetry.

Gearoid Mulvihill was awarded a Highly Commended distinction in the Literature category at the 2026 Global Undergraduate Awards ceremony held in Dublin on Thursday, October 8. 

Mulvihill is a graduate of MIC’s Bachelor of Arts programme, where he focused his undergraduate studies on Media and Communication Studies and English. Following the completion of his BA degree, he has remained at the Limerick college to undertake the Professional Master of Education in Primary Teaching.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362639.localAngle: The award-winning researcher is a graduate of Mary Immaculate College in Limerick and is currently studying there for his master's degree.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362639.originalTitle: Limerick student honoured for research on Irish hip-hop and poetry

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362636.headline: Gardaí issue fresh appeal over 2005 murder of Limerick man David Nunan
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362636.summary: Investigators have renewed calls for information on the 21st anniversary of the fatal shooting of 25-year-old David Nunan, whose body was found in Co Clare. Despite 17 arrests over two decades, no one has been charged.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362636.story:
Gardaí have made a fresh appeal for information regarding the unsolved murder of David Nunan, whose body was found on the outskirts of Limerick 21 years ago this week. The 25-year-old's body was discovered by a passer-by at Fairyhill, near the Fairyfield estate in Parteen, County Clare, on October 28, 2005. He had been shot twice in the back.

Investigators believe Mr Nunan received a phone call at around 2am in the early hours of the morning at his home in O’Malley Park, Southill. He was then collected by someone travelling in a wine Toyota Carina. According to Gardaí, the vehicle drove him from Southill to Moyross, and subsequently towards Parteen where the killing took place. Authorities are specifically appealing for information regarding the driver and any occupants of that car.

Over the course of the 21-year investigation, Gardaí have arrested 17 people and taken nearly 450 statements, though no charges have been brought. An incident room was originally established at Mayorstone Park Garda Station following the discovery of the body by a farmer tending to cattle.

Speaking previously about the ongoing pain caused by her son's death, Mr Nunan’s mother, Mary Nunan, appealed for justice, stating that the ordeal had been "hell" for her family. Anyone with information is asked to contact Mayorstone Garda Station on 061 456980, Henry Street Garda Station on 061 212400, the Garda Confidential Line on 1800 666 111, or any Garda station.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362636.localAngle: The victim was a Limerick native from Southill whose final movements before his murder in Co Clare began in Limerick City.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362636.originalTitle: Fresh appeal for information in 21 year old murder case

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362642.headline: CSO figures reveal 866 new homes completed across Limerick in 2025
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362642.summary: Central Statistics Office data shows that 866 new dwellings were finished in Limerick last year, including 500 scheme houses and 283 single houses. City West recorded the highest number of completions among local electoral areas.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362642.story:
A total of 866 new dwelling completions were recorded across Limerick in 2025, according to figures released by the Central Statistics Office (CSO).

Details of the housing output were provided to Fine Gael councillor Peter Doyle following a query to Limerick City and County Council. The local authority confirmed that the 2025 total comprised 500 scheme houses, 283 single houses, and 83 apartments.

A breakdown of the figures across Limerick's local electoral areas shows varied delivery rates. City West led the county with 251 completions, followed by City East with 193, and Adare-Rathkeale with 140. Further completions included 128 in Cappamore-Kilmallock, 108 in Newcastle West, and 46 in City North.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362642.localAngle: The figures provide a detailed breakdown of residential construction and housing delivery across Limerick's city and county electoral areas.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362642.originalTitle: Over 850 new dwellings completed in Limerick in 2025

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362653.headline: Keanes Jewellers Limerick Named Jewellery Store of the Year 2026
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362653.summary: Keanes Jewellers in Limerick has won the Jewellery Store of the Year title at the Elavon Retail Excellence Ireland Awards following a rigorous judging process.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362653.story:
Keanes Jewellers Limerick has taken home the title of Jewellery Store of the Year 2026 at the Elavon Retail Excellence Ireland Awards, marking a major national honour for the local business. The accolade follows an extensive judging process that included mystery shopping visits and an on-site evaluation by retail experts, including Matthew Brown from Echochamber and representatives from Retail Excellence Ireland.

“We are absolutely thrilled and honoured to receive this award,” said Patrick Keane, Director. “This is a tribute to our wonderful team in Limerick, who go above and beyond for every customer who walks through our doors. To be recognised by our industry on a national stage means the world to us.”

The award comes as the Limerick store prepares to celebrate its 25th anniversary in 2027, ahead of the wider company's 80th anniversary in 2028. The local branch recently underwent a major expansion and refurbishment in 2025 after acquiring the neighbouring former H. Samuel Jewellers building.

Mr Keane noted that the redesigned space was created to offer a modern, immersive luxury environment for local shoppers. “The city has been incredibly supportive of Keanes, and this renovation is both a thank you and a promise – we’re here for the long haul,” he added.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362653.localAngle: A prominent Limerick city centre jeweller has been recognised on the national stage for retail excellence.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362653.originalTitle: Keanes Jewellers crowned Jewellery Store of the Year

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53291.headline: Limerick claims nine spots on All-Star hurling team as Hegarty wins top award
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53291.summary: Limerick dominated the 2026 PwC GAA All-Star Awards with nine players named to the Hurling Team of the Year and Gearóid Hegarty crowned Hurler of the Year following their All-Ireland championship victory.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53291.story:
Limerick emerged as the dominant force at the PwC GAA All-Star Awards, securing nine places on the Hurling Team of the Year and seeing St Patrick’s clubman Gearóid Hegarty named Hurler of the Year.

The accolade marks Hegarty's fifth All-Star and his second Hurler of the Year title, having previously won both in 2020. He is joined in an all-Limerick half-forward line by teammates Cathal O’Neill and Aidan O’Connor. Meanwhile, Kyle Hayes claimed his sixth All-Star award, making him the first Limerick player to reach the milestone since legendary hurler Joe McKenna.

Goalkeeper Nickie Quaid secured his fourth All-Star, and Diarmaid Byrnes picked up his fifth. Barry Nash, William O’Donoghue, and midfielder Adam English also earned spots on the 2026 team. Despite missing out on several positions—with captain Cian Lynch, Sean Finn, Shane O’Brien, and Peter Casey among those bypassed—Limerick's total of nine representatives dwarfs the rest of the country, leaving Galway with three, Cork with two, and Clare with one.

The awards cap a remarkable turnaround for the Shannonsiders, who reclaimed the Liam MacCarthy Cup following the disappointment of their 2025 All-Ireland semi-final defeat to Cork.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53291.localAngle: The county's hurling success was celebrated with a dominant nine-player representation on the national All-Star team and the Hurler of the Year accolade for Gearóid Hegarty.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53291.originalTitle: Limerick dominate All-Star awards as Gearoid Hegarty crowned Hurler of The Year

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362659.headline: Limerick Council Rules Out Out-of-Hours Animal Welfare Service
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362659.summary: Fianna Fáil Councillor Catherine Slattery has called for an out-of-hours animal welfare officer in Limerick. However, the local authority stated it has no plans to appoint one, noting it lacks the statutory authority to enforce the relevant legislation.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362659.story:
Fianna Fáil councillor Catherine Slattery has called for the appointment of an out-of-hours animal welfare officer to handle local issues in Limerick. The proposal was raised during a recent full meeting of Limerick City and County Council.

In response to Cllr Slattery's appeal, the local authority stated that it does not currently have an authorised officer appointed under the Animal Health and Welfare Act 2013. Furthermore, the Council revealed it does not possess the statutory authority to enforce the provisions of the legislation.

The local authority confirmed that there are no current plans to appoint an authorised officer or establish an out-of-hours animal welfare service. According to the Council, responsibility for the implementation and enforcement of the Animal Health and Welfare Act 2013 rests primarily with the Department of Agriculture, Food, and the Marine.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362659.localAngle: The issue was raised by a local councillor at a full meeting of Limerick City and County Council regarding services within the local authority's jurisdiction.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362659.originalTitle: Calls for out-of-hours animal welfare officer

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362657.headline: Limerick train driver Jacqueline McMahon wins national Driver Excellence Award
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362657.summary: Limerick-based train driver Jacqueline McMahon has taken home the top prize at the annual Iarnród Éireann Customer Experience Excellence Awards, praised by colleagues for combining empathy with practical help.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362657.story:
A Limerick train driver has been recognised nationally for her exceptional service to rail passengers at the annual Iarnród Éireann Customer Experience Excellence Awards.

Jacqueline McMahon secured the Driver Excellence Award after being nominated by colleagues who highlighted her ability to combine empathy with practical help, stepping in to support passengers when they need it most.

Other Limerick staff also earned recognition at the national awards ceremony. Andressa Costa, a Customer Service Officer, was named as a finalist in the Onboard Staff category, while Kevin Maloney, Station Controller at Colbert Station, reached the finals in the Station Staff category.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362657.localAngle: Three Limerick-based rail workers were recognised for national excellence, including Colbert Station's station controller and an onboard customer service officer.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362657.originalTitle: Limerick train driver wins excellence award

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362695.headline: Garryowen's Gordon Wood to make first Munster start against Sharks at Thomond Park
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362695.summary: Academy centre Gordon Wood will make his first start for Munster in Saturday's United Rugby Championship clash against the Sharks at Thomond Park. Coach Clayton McMillan has named an exciting young backline for the 5.30pm fixture.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362695.story:
Garryowen clubman Gordon Wood is set for a milestone appearance this Saturday as he makes his first-ever start for Munster in their United Rugby Championship encounter with the Sharks. Kick-off at Thomond Park is scheduled for 5.30pm.

Munster coach Clayton McMillan praised the 22-year-old academy centre ahead of the game. "It will be a special day for Gordy making his first start for his home province as part of an exciting young backline. He is an impressive young man and we’re looking forward to seeing what he can do," McMillan said.

Alongside Wood, former Leinster player Rob Russell is handed his Munster debut on the wing. Other changes to the starting XV see Ben O’Donovan, JJ Hanrahan, Evan O’Connell, Seán Edogbo, and Brian Gleeson all brought into the lineup.

McMillan noted the team is eager to finish the opening block of fixtures with a strong home performance after working on improvements in the scrum, maul, and attack over the summer. Munster also welcomes Edwin Edogbo and Lee Barron back to the matchday mix following injury layoffs.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362695.localAngle: Local Garryowen product Gordon Wood makes his first starting appearance for his home province at Thomond Park.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362695.originalTitle: Academy centre makes first start for Munster

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362711.headline: Prospect man jailed for over two years after driving car into pedestrian in Hyde Avenue
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362711.summary: Michael Shannon, 31, was sentenced to two years and three months at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court after pleading guilty to affray and producing an iron bar during a violent feud-related incident on April 4, 2025.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362711.story:
A 31-year-old Limerick man who chased and drove a car into a pedestrian during a violent street altercation has been jailed for over two years at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court. Michael Shannon, of Lenihan Avenue, Prospect, pleaded guilty to charges of affray and producing an iron bar during the incident on Hyde Avenue on the south side of the city on April 4, 2025.

CCTV footage played in court captured Shannon and his passengers encountering another group of men near a pedestrian crossing. The footage showed an altercation during which one of the other men used an iron bar to smash the windscreen of Shannon’s Nissan Qashqai. Shannon subsequently left the scene, returned shortly afterwards, and drove at speed directly into the man who had broken his window, before colliding with another car. The injured man fled on foot, while Shannon drove away on the wrong side of the road.

Judge Colin Daly rejected Shannon's claim that the attack was unrelated to an ongoing local feud, noting that the accused's decision to return to the scene increased his culpability. Gardaí told the court the incident stemmed from a three-year feud between rival families in the Hyde Road area that has involved numerous violent episodes. Defence barrister Donal Cronin BL noted that Shannon had no previous convictions for violence, had apologized, accepted his behavior was wrong, and had since made peace with the other parties.

Judge Daly reduced Shannon's sentence from three years to two years and three months, taking into account his guilty plea, lack of violent history, and the fact that he is a father of five who has been employed for the past two years. Shannon has over twenty previous convictions, including for road traffic offences, burglary, handling stolen property, and drug possession.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362711.localAngle: The violent incident occurred on Hyde Avenue and was linked by Gardaí to an ongoing local feud in the area.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362711.originalTitle: Jail for man who drove car into pedestrian

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362661.headline: Dromin-Athlacca Bounce Back to Senior Hurling with Final Win Over Bruff
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362661.summary: Dromin-Athlacca secured an immediate return to senior hurling with a 2-18 to 3-11 victory over Bruff in the Premier Intermediate Final at the Gaelic Grounds. James Kennedy's side laid the foundations for the win with a commanding ten-point lead at half-time.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362661.story:
Dromin-Athlacca made a swift return to senior hurling on Saturday, overcoming local rivals Bruff 2-18 to 3-11 in the Premier Intermediate Final at the Gaelic Grounds. 

Benefiting from the tail end of Storm Boelo, James Kennedy’s side stormed into a commanding ten-point lead by the interval, ahead 2-11 to 0-7. First-half goals from man of the match David Breen and Jack Fitzgibbon, alongside reliable scoring from David Reidy, put the team firmly in control during the opening 30 minutes.

Bruff mounted a spirited comeback in the second half with green flags from Paul Browne and Seán Finn, ensuring a tense finish, but Dromin-Athlacca successfully kept their opponents at arm's length to seal the title. Approaching their 75th Diamond Anniversary, the winning club will be led once again next season by Breen and Shane Scully.

Elsewhere across the weekend's county hurling deciders, Knockaderry claimed back-to-back titles with a 1-16 to 0-17 win over Bruree in the Intermediate Final. Doon captured the Premier Junior A crown by defeating Caherline 3-12 to 0-10, while Monagea swept past Killeedy 2-14 to 1-6 to take the Junior A title at Newcastle West. Additional silverware was collected by Patrickswell, Cappamore, Garryspillane, and Effin.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362661.localAngle: The Premier Intermediate Final at the Gaelic Grounds saw two neighboring Limerick clubs battle for a return to senior hurling ranks.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362661.originalTitle: Quick return to senior for Dromin-Athlacca

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362667.headline: New Found Footage Horror Movie 'Infirmary' Lands on Shudder Streaming Service
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362667.summary: Director Nicholas Pineda's new found-footage horror film, Infirmary, is now streaming on Shudder. The psychiatric hospital-set movie has received a two-out-of-five star review for relying too heavily on established genre tropes.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362667.story:
Horror fans looking for a new scare on streaming services can now catch Infirmary, which has officially landed on the Shudder platform. Directed by Nicholas Pineda, the latest entry into the found-footage sub-genre takes place in the creepy corridors of an abandoned psychiatric hospital.

Drawing comparisons to genre staples like Hell House LLC and The Backrooms, the film follows a point-and-shoot surveillance style featuring disquieting mannequins moving through darkened rooms. Reviewers note that while the production gets the heart racing with enthusiastic scares, it ultimately offers little that is original to veteran horror enthusiasts who have seen similar shaky-camera offerings before.

Critics have awarded the movie a modest two out of five stars, suggesting that while it ticks all the right boxes for an atmospheric scare—complete with old psychiatric hospital settings and wandering mannequins—it leans too heavily on copying homework from brighter sparks in the supernatural found-footage genre.

For local film enthusiasts browsing the Shudder platform this week, Infirmary is available to watch now, offering a familiar brand of spooky surveillance thrills for those willing to brave the dark.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362667.localAngle: The new film release is available for streaming to horror film fans across Limerick via the Shudder platform.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362664.headline: Newcastle West puppy crowned Munster winner at Petmania Puppy of the Year 2026
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362664.summary: Sullivan, a Golden Retriever-Cocker Spaniel cross from Newcastle West, has taken the Munster title at the Petmania Puppy of the Year 2026 competition. He was chosen from 1,414 entries across Ireland after reaching the Grand Final in Dublin.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362664.story:
A Limerick puppy has officially settled the debate on who is the best boy after being crowned the Munster winner at the Petmania Puppy of the Year 2026.

Sullivan, a Golden Retriever-Cocker Spaniel cross from Newcastle West, secured the regional title after making it through as one of 26 county finalists at the Grand Final. The event took place at the Pet Expo in the National Show Centre in Dublin earlier this month and was hosted by Eurovision winner and animal welfare advocate Linda Martin. The 11th annual competition drew 1,414 entries from across the country.

Owned by Marie Carr O’Kelly and her husband Patrick, Sullivan is well known locally as the head bar manager in the Silver Dollar Bar, named after a loyal customer and friend. He also serves as a mascot for the Newcastle West Senior Camogie team.

"We entered a number of local dog competitions, which he thoroughly enjoyed, and when I saw the Petmania Puppy of the Year competition, I wasted no time and entered him!" owner Marie Carr O’Kelly said. "He is known and loved by all customers, Sullivan gives special individual time to everyone. When he hears car keys he sits at the front door and waits. No car leaves without him."
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362664.localAngle: Sullivan is a local rescue and community favourite from Newcastle West who represented Limerick on the national stage.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362664.originalTitle: Sullivan crowned the best boy in all of Munster

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362673.headline: Light Up Limerick Christmas celebrations and fireworks display confirmed for November 21
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362673.summary: Light Up Limerick will officially kick off the city's festive season on Saturday, November 21, featuring a procession by LUXE, live entertainment, and a fireworks display on O'Connell Street.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362673.story:
Christmas in Limerick will officially begin on Saturday, November 21, with the return of the annual Light Up Limerick ceremony. The free public event will transform the city centre from 7pm with a festive procession produced by LUXE, departing from Brown Thomas and making its way along O'Connell Street.

 Spectators can expect illuminated characters, live music, street performances, and seasonal entertainment. The procession will guide crowds toward a specially constructed stage at the top of O'Connell Street, which will host live performances and special guests ahead of the official switch-on ceremony, culminating in a musical finale and fireworks display.

 Organizers advise attendees to gather along O'Connell Street between Brown Thomas and Lower Glentworth Street from 6.30pm to 7pm for the best views. The event marks the official launch of the Christmas in Limerick 2026 programme, with further details on seasonal events to be announced in the coming weeks.

 Mayor of Limerick John Moran said that the switch-on marks the true start of Christmas for many and offers a chance for people of all ages to celebrate in the heart of the city. "From the spectacular procession and switch-on ceremony to the many events and experiences that will follow throughout the Christmas period, we look forward to welcoming residents and visitors alike to Limerick for what promises to be a memorable Christmas," he said.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362673.localAngle: The annual festive event marks the official start of the Christmas season in Limerick city centre.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362670.headline: Askeaton triple transplant survivor Robert Sheahan urges organ donation amid falling rates
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362670.summary: Seven years after becoming the first person in Ireland to receive a historic double-lung and liver transplant, County Limerick man Robert Sheahan is calling on the public to consider becoming organ donors as donation numbers fall.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362670.story:
Seven years after undergoing a historic, pioneering triple transplant at Dublin's Mater Hospital, Askeaton native Robert Sheahan is urging the public to consider organ donation as rates across the country experience a sharp decline.

In his 20s, the cystic fibrosis sufferer was given just six weeks to live before surgeons from Dublin’s Mater Hospital and St Vincent’s University Hospital joined forces in June 2019 to perform Ireland's first-ever double-lung and liver operation in a single procedure. Now 36 and working as a clerical officer at Limerick City and County Council, Sheahan is speaking out about the drop in available organs.

"There has been a real shortage of organ donations, so there is a real need for people to be organ donors," Sheahan said, adding that the decline is a major concern as transplant surgeries fall simply because fewer organs are being donated. Figures show that organ transplants dropped to 202 in 2025, down from 263 in 2024 and 265 in 2023.

Reflecting on his journey, Sheahan recalled the severe hurdles he faced before the surgery, including failing liver function and diminished lung capacity that left him dependent on insulin for Type 1 diabetes and needing an oxygen tank. Physical preparation through powerlifting at a Limerick city gym helped him build his strength while awaiting the historic call for surgery.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362670.localAngle: Askeaton native and Limerick City and County Council employee Robert Sheahan is highlighting falling organ donation rates seven years after his historic transplant.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362670.originalTitle: Triple transplant patient taking home swimming medals

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362677.headline: Clareview’s James McCarthy and Ballingarry’s Maurice Noonan named in Ireland Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup squad
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362677.summary: Two Limerick men will represent Ireland at the 2026 Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup in Australia. James McCarthy makes his second World Cup appearance, while Maurice Noonan features for the first time.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362677.story:
Limerick men James McCarthy of Clareview and Ballingarry’s Maurice Noonan have been selected to represent Ireland at the upcoming 2026 Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup in Australia. 

Wheelchair rugby league is a fast, physical, and tactical mixed-gender sport played on a 40m by 20m court with five players per team using sports wheelchairs. Ireland enters the tournament ranked third in the world behind England and France, following three consecutive Celtic Cup titles. 

"To be honest, it’s a huge personal achievement," said Maurice Noonan. "To represent one’s country at the highest possible level is surreal. It’s great that James is so close to me here in Limerick, and we have worked very well with the rest of the squad over the last while, and feel that we are in a good position heading Down Under." Both players have also recently featured for Munster, winning the Inter-provincial Wheelchair Hurling Championship.

Ireland has been drawn in a group alongside Wales, England, and the United States, with their opening match against the US scheduled at the WIN Entertainment Centre in Wollongong on Friday at 2am Irish Time. The eight-nation tournament concludes with semi-finals and finals in mid-November, and all fixtures will be broadcast live on Premier Sports.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362677.localAngle: Local sportsmen James McCarthy from Clareview and Maurice Noonan from Ballingarry have been selected to play for the Irish national team on the world stage.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362677.originalTitle: World Cup adventure for Limerick Pair

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362685.headline: Speed Fibre Group volunteers repaint Focus Ireland's Castletroy offices
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362685.summary: Employees from Speed Fibre Group have given the Limerick branch of Focus Ireland a complete refresh, repainting the halls and rooms throughout the Castletroy building.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362685.story:
The Limerick office of Focus Ireland in Castletroy has received a fresh coat of paint thanks to a team of volunteers from Speed Fibre Group. Staff from the digital infrastructure investor stepped in to source new paint and tackle the interior of the building, refreshing the halls and rooms used by the charity.

The makeover forms part of the company's ongoing support for Focus Ireland. Alongside the painting initiative, the group is also involved with the charity's annual Christmas Shoebox Appeal.

Focus Ireland operates as a housing and homelessness charity, working locally and nationally to prevent people from becoming, remaining, or returning to homelessness. The organization provides a range of quality services, supported housing, research, and advocacy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362685.localAngle: The volunteer effort directly benefits the Castletroy-based branch of Focus Ireland, which provides vital housing and homelessness services to the Limerick community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362685.originalTitle: Lick of paint gives Limerick branch of Focus Ireland a new boost

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362683.headline: Shannon Airport Named Best Under-5-Million Passenger Airport at Global Routes Awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362683.summary: Shannon Airport has won the 'Under 5 Million Passengers' category at the Routes World Awards 2026 in Frankfurt, emerging as the sole Irish winner.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362683.story:
Shannon Airport has secured a major international accolade after being named the winner in the “Under 5 Million Passengers” category at the Routes World Awards 2026. Announced in Frankfurt, the airport was the only Irish facility recognised at this year's event.

Shannon triumphed over a shortlist that included Bratislava Airport, Cardiff Airport, Cork Airport, and Canada's Halifax Stanfield International Airport. The global award honours excellence in route development, aviation marketing, and airline partnerships, with winners determined by airlines themselves.

The airport's winning submission highlighted a 12 per cent surge in passenger numbers during the first half of 2026 and the expansion of its network to 40 services—the highest number operated from Shannon in 17 years. Recent additions include new routes to Rome, Madrid, Warsaw, Poznań, and Frankfurt, alongside an upcoming Air Canada service to Toronto slated for Summer 2027.

Ray O’Driscoll, CEO of The Shannon Airport Group, said the recognition reflected the strength and potential of the region. Declan Power, Head of Aviation Development at the airport, added that the award serves as a strong endorsement of the collaborative approach taken with airline partners to deliver for both carriers and passengers.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362683.localAngle: The global aviation award highlights Shannon Airport's growth and its direct economic and tourism benefits for the local region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362683.originalTitle: Shannon wins Global Routes World Award

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362681.headline: Agri Aware Wins State Contract to Deliver Farm Safety Program in Secondary Schools
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362681.summary: Following a competitive tender process, Agri Aware has been awarded a contract to run the Farm Safety First Programme in second-level schools across the country. The initiative comes after two fatal farm accidents occurred in Limerick over the past year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362681.story:
Agri Aware has secured the contract to promote farm safety awareness in second-level schools following a competitive tender process. The educational initiative, known as the Farm Safety First Programme, includes an option to extend the agreement annually up to 2031.

The announcement comes during a year that has seen two people lose their lives in farm accidents in Limerick. Across the country, figures show that eight people under the age of 18 have died on Irish farms over the past decade, with every single one of those fatalities involving farm vehicles.

Minister of State for Forestry, Farm Safety, and Horticulture, Niall Collins, welcomed the funding. He noted that the program will assist secondary teachers in educating students about the hazards associated with agriculture and urged schools to embrace the training.

Agri Aware Chair Shay Galvin highlighted that while farming is a rewarding environment, it carries distinct risks. He explained that the Farm Safety First programme provides classroom resources alongside practical elements, including in-person workshops and farm visits, to promote best practices and reduce future accidents.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362681.localAngle: The rollout of the national farm safety school program follows a year in which two people lost their lives in farm accidents within Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362681.originalTitle: Training in farm safety for schools and young people

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362731.headline: Sixty beds sit empty near overcrowded UHL as patient demand surges
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362731.summary: University Hospital Limerick has seen over 2,370 additional patient attendances this year, while 60 state-of-the-art intermediary care beds remain vacant just 1.8km away at Raheen Lodge due to ongoing contract delays with the HSE.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362731.story:
University Hospital Limerick is facing a severe capacity crunch as patient attendances rise by more than 2,370 compared to last year. Meanwhile, 60 en-suite beds lie empty just 1.8 kilometres away at the privately owned Raheen Lodge facility in Limerick, awaiting a contract agreement with the HSE.

Built by Bartra Healthcare at a cost of €20 million, the 80-bed unit opened last May and currently has only 20 beds in use. Chief Executive Angela Ring expressed frustration that the facility's on-site doctor, nurses, therapists, and ambulance transport are sitting ready with up to 30 staff on standby while bureaucratic delays drag on. The beds are intended to serve as a vital step-down release valve for five regional hospitals, including UHL, St John's, and Croom.

According to Bartra's analysis of HSE figures, an average of 38 acute beds across the mid-west were occupied daily this year by patients medically approved for discharge, including 25 at UHL alone. This bottleneck has created knock-on effects that leave over 8,000 adult patients waiting on average each month for appointments across the region.

The HSE Mid West acknowledged the profound capacity crisis in a recent statement, noting that hospital staff are working under unprecedented pressure and that rising demand has significantly reduced the system's ability to accommodate new patients. However, the health service declined to specifically address questions regarding the facility or the sudden cancellation of a March tender for transitional care beds.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362731.localAngle: The ongoing overcrowding crisis directly impacts patients across Limerick and the wider mid-west region attending University Hospital Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362731.originalTitle: Record demand for beds in UHL while 60 beds lie empty in nearby facility

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362717.headline: Mayor John Moran commits €10,000 to save Moyross school breakfast club
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362717.summary: Limerick Mayor John Moran has allocated €10,000 from the Mayoral Fund to St. Munchin’s Community Centre, securing its school breakfast programme for over 200 children for the coming year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362717.story:
Mayor of Limerick John Moran has stepped in to rescue a Moyross school food programme by committing €10,000 from the Mayoral Fund, subject to necessary funding approvals. The vital funding will keep St. Munchin’s Community Centre's breakfast club running for the next 12 months.

The centre’s breakfast club opens at 8am each day, feeding more than 200 children before school in partnership with local primary schools, including Corpus Christi Primary School. For many of the participating children, the freshly cooked meal provided by qualified chefs is their main meal of the day. 

Linda Ledger, CEO of St. Munchin’s Community Centre, had alerted the Mayor that the service faced immediate closure after Halloween due to severe financial pressures and shortfalls in government funding. The centre had previously covered the funding gaps from its own resources.

Mayor Moran stated that children cannot learn on an empty stomach and that school meals are a health equity issue. "This money gives schools and families certainty now and gives us time to work on a lasting solution with the centre and its partners," he said.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362717.localAngle: The funding directly protects a crucial daily breakfast service for more than 200 children attending local primary schools in Moyross.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362717.originalTitle: Mayor cooks up a full Irish for Moyross kids

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362688.headline: Southill Hub Secures Vhi Funding for Youth Nutrition Programme
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362688.summary: The Limerick community organisation has received funding from the Vhi Health and Wellbeing Fund 2026. The money will support interactive cooking workshops for young people.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362688.story:
Southill Hub in Limerick City has been announced as one of the beneficiaries of this year’s Vhi Health and Wellbeing Fund. The local organisation was among nine youth groups and community organisations across Ireland to share a total of €85,000 in funding.

The financial boost will directly support the hub’s ‘Nurture Through Nutrition’ programme. The initiative delivers interactive health cooking and nutrition workshops tailored for young people aged 12 to 25.

Organisers designed the programme to help participants develop practical food skills and make informed dietary choices, while also addressing food poverty in the area. Representatives from Southill Hub recently celebrated the funding announcement alongside corporate representatives from Vhi.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362688.localAngle: The funding directly supports a youth programme based at the Southill Hub in Limerick City.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362688.originalTitle: Southill Hub receive boost from VHI fund

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53393.headline: Mid-West Homeless Figures Surge by 34% as NOVAS Issues Winter Warning
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53393.summary: Department of Housing figures show adult emergency accommodation in the Mid-West rose to 807 in August 2026, while homeless families increased by 50.3%. Charity NOVAS warns services are facing extreme pressure as winter approaches.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53393.story:
Homelessness services across the Mid-West are facing unprecedented pressure as winter approaches, with charity provider NOVAS reporting that national and regional statistics are rising at an alarming rate. Department of Housing figures reveal that the number of adults accessing state-funded emergency accommodation in the region jumped by 34.3%, climbing from 601 in August 2025 to 807 in August 2026. Over the same period, the number of homeless families surged by 50.3%, rising from 153 to 230.

NOVAS stressed that these figures fail to capture the full extent of the crisis, excluding rough sleepers, people sofa-surfing, and those experiencing hidden homelessness. The charity highlighted a growing cohort of employed individuals who are unable to secure affordable housing due to rising living costs and housing insecurity. "Employment should provide a route to housing security, but having a job does not necessarily mean someone can find accommodation they can afford," NOVAS stated.

As temperatures drop, demand for local services—particularly the evening street outreach on Upper William Street—is expected to grow. Operating every evening at 7pm, the outreach team provides hot meals, basic first aid, sleeping bags, and toiletries. However, the charity warned that significant gaps remain in emergency accommodation despite winter support initiatives run in collaboration with the Limerick Homeless Action Team at Limerick City and County Council.

In response to the mounting crisis, NOVAS is appealing to the Limerick public for financial donations and essential items. The charity's current winter appeal is seeking new and unused toiletries, women's clothing, sleeping bags, and treats, alongside support for its upcoming annual 'Christmas Sleep Out' in December.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53393.localAngle: The surge in Mid-West homelessness and the ongoing operations of local outreach services directly impact vulnerable individuals and community support networks across Limerick City and County.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53393.originalTitle: BREAKING: Homelessness rising at an ‘alarming rate’

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362726.headline: Over 800 homes and businesses in Newcastle West connected to high-speed broadband
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362726.summary: National Broadband Ireland has completed works bringing high-speed fibre broadband to more than 800 premises in the Newcastle West area, including Glensharrold, Fleanmore, Loughill, and Kilmoylan.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362726.story:
More than 800 homes and businesses in Newcastle West can now access high-speed fibre broadband following the completion of the latest rollout phase by National Broadband Ireland (NBI). 

Announced on behalf of the government, the newly completed works directly benefit residents and businesses based in the rural areas of Glensharrold, Fleanmore, Loughill, and Kilmoylan. 

This latest milestone brings the total number of premises able to pre-order or order high-speed, reliable broadband across County Limerick to 21,937. To date, 7,229 connections have been successfully made.

NBI confirmed that construction works have already been finished in several other rural parts of the county, including Abbeyfeale and Newport. Residents across Limerick are being encouraged to check their Eircodes on the NBI website to confirm if their premises are ready to connect.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362726.localAngle: The rollout directly impacts rural communities across County Limerick, improving digital connectivity for over 800 premises in the Newcastle West area.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362726.originalTitle: Over homes in Newcastle West can now avail of high-speed broadband

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53385.headline: Limerick CCTV usage jumps 85% as council faces €660,000 funding shortfall for 2027
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53385.summary: CCTV footage activity across Limerick increased by 85% this year, with over 488 hours recorded in August alone. However, the network faces a projected shortfall of approximately €660,000 for next year.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53385.story:
CCTV footage activity across Limerick City has surged by 85% compared to the same period in 2025, according to data presented to Limerick City and County Council.

During a special council meeting on September 15, figures revealed that over 488 hours of footage were recorded in August following 36 requests. Limerick City accounted for the vast majority with 395 hours, while County Limerick recorded 92 hours. Council officials noted that the data reflects an increase in recorded activity rather than a rise in crime or footage requests.

The figures come amid ongoing uncertainty regarding the future of the monitoring service, which costs an estimated €1.21 million annually to operate. With funding for 2027 currently standing at €550,105, the network faces a projected shortfall of roughly €660,000. The issue was raised in Dáil Éireann on October 7 by Sinn Féin TD Maurice Quinlivan, who questioned government funding and raised concerns about staff at the Moyross monitoring centre being placed on protective leave.

Social Democrats Councillor Shane Hickey O’Mara stressed that continued funding for the system must be ringfenced by central government rather than local authorities. "It is not the mayor’s job to fund this network; it is the role of the government to listen and for our local TDs to advocate for this with their colleagues who hold the purse strings," he said, warning that relying on local mayoral funds would cause other initiatives to suffer.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53385.localAngle: The story directly impacts Limerick residents and communities relying on the city and county's CCTV monitoring network for public safety.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53385.originalTitle: CCTV footage activity increases by 85% in Limerick as funding remains uncertain

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362724.headline: McSweeney seeks council funding for Patrickswell pedestrian crossings
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362724.summary: Fine Gael Councillor Dan McSweeney has called on Limerick City and County Council to apply for grant funding to install improved pedestrian crossings at two busy locations in Patrickswell. In response, the local authority's Active Travel team will examine the feasibility of a 2027 application.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362724.story:
Fine Gael councillor Dan McSweeney has asked Limerick City and County Council (LCCC) to seek grant funding for improved pedestrian crossing facilities at two key locations in Patrickswell. 

During the October meeting of the Metropolitan District, Cllr McSweeney tabled a formal motion proposing that the Council apply for funding to install better crossing facilities, along with appropriate signage and road markings. The specific spots identified are the bus stop near the Well Done Chinese Takeaway and the Patrickswell Community Centre on Main Street.

Highlighting the need for the upgrades, Cllr McSweeney pointed to rising traffic volumes moving through the village. “Both of these locations experience significant pedestrian activity, particularly around the bus stop and Patrickswell Community Centre, and I believe there is a strong case for providing improved crossing facilities at these locations,” he said.

In response to the motion, the Council’s Active Travel team stated it will consult with the Operations and Maintenance Team regarding the requirements for the sites. The local authority will also look into the feasibility of submitting a funding application under the Towns and Villages scheme for 2027.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362724.localAngle: The proposed infrastructure upgrades directly impact pedestrian safety and traffic management for residents and visitors traveling through Patrickswell village.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362724.originalTitle: McSweeney calls for improved pedestrian crossings in Patrickswell

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362722.headline: Former Limerick Chamber CEO Donnacha Hurley appointed General Manager of Strand Hotel
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362722.summary: Ballykeeffe native Donnacha Hurley has taken over as General Manager of the four-star Limerick Strand Hotel, succeeding the late Stephen O'Connor. Hurley brings over 25 years of hospitality experience to the MHL Hotel Collection property.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362722.story:
The Limerick Strand Hotel has announced the appointment of Donnacha Hurley as its new General Manager. Hurley takes over the role at the four-star riverside hotel following a 17-year tenure leading the Absolute Hotel Limerick and a recent stint as Chief Executive of Limerick Chamber.

He succeeds the late Stephen O'Connor, whose leadership left a lasting legacy at the property. Appointed by MHL Hotel Collection partners John Lally and Paul Higgins, Hurley will oversee all hotel operations, including the River Bar & Restaurant, conference facilities, and the Energize Health Club.

A native of Ballykeeffe and a graduate of the Shannon College of Hotel Management, Hurley has held hospitality roles across Ireland, the UK, and Switzerland. His career includes management positions in Manchester and London, alongside leadership roles with the Irish Hotels Federation and Discover Limerick DAC.

Speaking on his appointment, Hurley said: "My time with Limerick Chamber was a privilege, but leading The Limerick Strand Hotel felt like coming home. With significant investment in Limerick and the Ryder Cup at Adare Manor on the horizon, there are exciting opportunities ahead for both the hotel and the region."
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362722.localAngle: A native of Ballykeeffe, local hospitality veteran Donnacha Hurley returns to hotel management in Limerick after serving as Chief Executive of Limerick Chamber.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362722.originalTitle: Hurley takes the reins at Strand Hotel

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53429.headline: New Learner Permit Rules Limit Drivers to Two Permits Before Test
