https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53429.summary: Stricter regulations introduced on November 1 restrict learner drivers to two permits before taking their driving test. Motorists seeking a third or fourth permit must now provide proof of a test taken within the last two years.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53429.story:
Stricter regulations for learner drivers came into effect on November 1, limiting motorists to a maximum of two learner permits before they must take their driving test. Under the new rules, anyone applying to renew a third or fourth permit must provide proof that they have sat a driving test within the past two years. Furthermore, drivers who fail to pass their test after seven years will no longer be able to renew their learner permits and must restart the licensing process from the very beginning.

James Dillon, a driving instructor with Adare Drive Wise School of Motoring, told the Limerick Voice that the changes place greater pressure on learner drivers to progress through the system. Noting that there has been an excessive number of learner permit holders over the past 15 years, Dillon said the update tackles an area where motorists previously stalled. “This is an area where learner permit holders weren’t bothering. They’re now being forced to do it,” he said.

While the regulations aim to push drivers through the licensing process, learner drivers must still pass their theory test before receiving a permit and complete 12 Essential Driver Training (EDT) lessons prior to applying for a test. Meanwhile, waiting lists remain prolonged, with Category B test applicants currently facing estimated invitation dates as late as the end of January.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53429.localAngle: Local driving instructors in Limerick report that the stricter regulations will increase pressure on motorists across the county to progress through the licensing system.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53429.originalTitle: Changes made to learner permit renewal for drivers

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53426.headline: Corbally United AFC Calls for New Limerick Centre of Excellence
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53426.summary: Corbally United AFC is pushing for a new Centre of Excellence in Limerick to address a shortage of all-weather pitches. As clubs weigh up options for the Community Sports Facilities Fund, officials say grassroots football needs shared multi-pitch facilities to survive winter weather.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53426.story:
Corbally United AFC is urging authorities to develop a dedicated Centre of Excellence for Limerick football to solve a chronic shortage of all-weather training facilities. One month after the opening of the Community Sports Facilities Fund (CSFF), club officials are weighing how to spend potential grants, with Corbally currently investigating the feasibility of installing a full-size astroturf pitch.

Club Secretary Colm McLoughlin said grassroots football across the city cannot rely on rented university spaces or existing grass pitches, which are heavily worn down by winter weather. Pointing out that there are only three astroturf pitches currently in the city, McLoughlin argued that long-term planning is essential for the next generation of players.

To ease the pressure on individual clubs, McLoughlin has proposed a central facility featuring four to five pitches, combining both astroturf and grass surfaces. He noted that while Limerick District League Junior Football uses Jackman Park, the Limerick District Schoolchildren League currently lacks a permanent home of its own.

Applications for the CSFF remain open until February 26, 2027. Minister for Culture, Communications and Sport Patrick O’Donovan TD previously noted that the funding includes a €750,000 tier specifically designed for larger, shared facilities involving local authorities and national governing bodies.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53426.localAngle: The proposed Centre of Excellence would directly serve Limerick District League and Schoolchildren League clubs struggling with a lack of all-weather pitches in the city.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53426.originalTitle: ‘We need a Centre of Excellence’ – Corbally United AFC

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362746.headline: Limerick Woman Murder Investigation Launched After Enniskillen Disappearance
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362746.summary: A 35-year-old man has been arrested in Northern Ireland on suspicion of murder following the disappearance of 39-year-old Carrie Mullane (Noonan) from Limerick. She was last seen in Enniskillen on October 10.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362746.story:
A murder investigation has been launched by the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) following the disappearance of 39-year-old Limerick woman Carrie Mullane (Noonan), with a 35-year-old man arrested on suspicion of murder.

Ms Mullane travelled to Enniskillen, Co Fermanagh, by bus on October 10 alongside a man known to her. The pair took a taxi from the Wellington Road bus depot to an address in Trasna Park. Her last confirmed sighting was at approximately 9pm that Saturday, and there have been no confirmed sightings or contact with family since. An Garda Síochána reported concerns for her wellbeing to the PSNI on October 29, prompting an intensive missing person search involving CCTV trawls and house-to-house inquiries.

Detective Superintendent Richard Thornton of the Serious Crime Branch stated that her disappearance is highly out of character, noting that she was usually in daily contact with her loved ones. "These enquiries to date have not established her whereabouts and have led us to hold serious concern that Carrie may have been the victim of a violent crime and may in fact have been murdered sometime after her arrival in Northern Ireland," he said. PSNI Family Liaison Officers have travelled to Limerick to support Ms Mullane's family.

Investigators are urging anyone with information regarding Ms Mullane's movements on the weekend of October 10 or afterwards to contact the PSNI's Major Investigation Team on 101, quoting reference number 272 29/10/26.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362746.localAngle: The missing woman is a 39-year-old from Limerick, and PSNI family liaison officers have travelled to the city to support her relatives.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362746.originalTitle: Man arrested on suspicion of murder following disappearance of Limerick woman

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362744.headline: Trial hears 89-year-old Josie Ray fought back before being strangled to death in bed
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362744.summary: The Central Criminal Court heard closing arguments in the murder trial of Hasan Ali Gori, who is accused of killing 89-year-old Josie Ray in Nenagh in August 2024. The prosecution told the jury that the grandmother suffered 44 bruises and two broken neck bones while trying to defend herself.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362744.story:
The Central Criminal Court heard on Tuesday that 89-year-old grandmother Josie Ray died trying to defend herself as she was being strangled in her bed. Closing the prosecution's case, senior counsel Lorcan Connolly told the jury of nine men and three women that the "only appropriate verdict is guilty" for 52-year-old Hasan Ali Gori, who denies murdering Ms Ray on August 4, 2024.

Mr Connolly detailed the extent of the victim's injuries, noting that the Nenagh pensioner suffered two broken neck bones alongside 44 bruises across her head, neck, face, shoulders, chest, arms, and legs. The court heard that tensions had escalated in the St Joseph’s Park home after Mr Gori moved in with Ms Ray and her daughter Mary, a vulnerable adult with an intellectual disability. Prosecutors argued that Mr Gori had both motive and opportunity, pointing to financial gains and friction over his status as a tenant in the local authority-owned property.

Despite her age, the prosecution argued that "Josie Ray didn’t go down without a fight," citing defensive bruising on her arms and DNA evidence recovered under her fingernails. Defence arguments noted that DNA transfer could occur in shared accommodation without direct contact. The trial before the Central Criminal Court in Limerick continues as the jury considers its verdict.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362744.localAngle: The high-profile murder trial is being heard at the Central Criminal Court sitting in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362744.originalTitle: Grandmother died trying to defend herself jury told

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53423.headline: University of Limerick graduate Noel McNamara appointed new Leinster head coach
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53423.summary: UL alumnus Noel McNamara will take over as Leinster head coach ahead of the 2027/28 season, replacing Leo Cullen. The 43-year-old Clare native currently serves as attack coach for European champions Union Bordeaux-Bègles.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53423.story:
University of Limerick graduate Noel McNamara has been confirmed as Leinster’s next head coach, taking over the role from Leo Cullen for the 2027/28 season. The 43-year-old is currently the attack coach for European champions Union Bordeaux-Bègles.

McNamara, a native of O’Callaghan’s Mills in Clare, studied Maths and PE at the University of Limerick before embarking on a teaching career at Glenstal Abbey and Clongowes Wood College. During his career, he has held coaching roles with Leinster Rugby, UCD, and the IRFU, alongside serving as Ireland Under-20s head coach from 2017 to 2021—winning a Grand Slam in 2019—and Leinster’s academy manager.

His appointment at Leinster is expected to bring a shift towards a more attacking style of play, succeeding Cullen and senior coach Jacques Nienaber. Since joining Bordeaux in 2023, McNamara has helped the club secure back-to-back European titles in 2025 and 2026, which included a 41-19 victory over Leinster in the 2026 final and a record-breaking 163 tries last season.

IRFU Performance Director David Humphreys led the recruitment process over recent months. McNamara's success following his departure from Ireland echoes the trajectories of Felix Jones and Ronan O’Gara, leaving some Munster supporters frustrated that such coaching talent has not been secured by their home province.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53423.localAngle: The newly appointed Leinster head coach is a graduate of the University of Limerick, where he studied Maths and PE.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53423.originalTitle: UL alum confirmed to take over as Leinster head coach

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362728.headline: Aware launches weekly mental health peer support meetings at Mary Immaculate College
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362728.summary: The Limerick branch of Aware has launched regular support and self-care meetings for people experiencing depression or bipolar disorder. The confidential sessions take place on the first three Tuesdays of every month at Mary Immaculate College.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362728.story:
A voluntary mental health organisation has resumed regular face-to-face meetings in Limerick to provide support for individuals experiencing depression or bipolar disorder, as well as their loved ones.

Aware is running its Support and Self Care Groups to offer a confidential and proactive environment where attendees can talk openly about mood conditions and their impact. During the sessions, participants share personal experiences, understanding, and practical techniques for building resilience and managing self-care.

The Limerick branch meetings take place on the first three Tuesdays of every month. Sessions are held at 7pm on the ground floor in Room G08 of the Foundation Building at Mary Immaculate College.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362728.localAngle: The weekly support groups provide an accessible, local resource for Limerick residents dealing with depression or bipolar disorder.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362728.originalTitle: Mental health peer support group resume meetings

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53439.headline: Cllr Hickey-O’Mara Calls for Council AI Policy Following €4,000 Christmas Video
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53439.summary: Limerick County Council faces criticism from councillors and students after paying a German company €4,000 for an AI-generated Christmas tourism video, prompting calls for a strict artificial intelligence policy.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53439.story:
Limerick County Council is facing fresh pressure to establish a formal artificial intelligence policy following the release of an AI-generated promotional video for Christmas in Limerick. 

The video, posted a month ago on the official Limerick Festivals and Events social media accounts, was produced by German firm Render Vision at a cost of €4,000. While the Council disabled the comments section on the post, public backlash and criticism from sitting councillors quickly followed.

Cllr Shane Hickey-O’Mara has led the calls for accountability, telling the Limerick Voice that the priority is to introduce clear guidelines on whether and when AI content can be used by the local authority. He noted the frustration of funding an overseas tech company at a time when local arts and culture initiatives struggle to secure council support for Limerick-based artists.

Local students have also weighed in on the growing reliance on AI by public bodies and businesses across the city. University of Limerick student Brian Kelly expressed concern that such technology displaces opportunities for creative media students, adding that AI content often lacks the viewer retention of human-made work. The Limerick County Council is currently preparing a statement in response to the backlash.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53439.localAngle: The controversy centres on how Limerick County Council spends public funds and promotes local tourism and creative talent.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53439.originalTitle: Local councillor speaks on AI advertising dominating Limerick’s businesses

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362720.headline: Limerick FC launches heritage website ahead of club's 90th anniversary
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362720.summary: A new temporary microsite has been launched as Limerick FC prepares for its return next season, marking 90 years since the club's foundation in 1937. The hub will provide information and partnership opportunities ahead of a main website launch later this year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362720.story:
A new online hub has been unveiled to provide information ahead of the return of Limerick FC next season. The temporary website, www.limerickfcheritage.com, will serve as a central information point before the club launches its main website later this year.

Next year marks 90 years since Limerick FC was founded in 1937. The upcoming Heritage Season aims to celebrate local football traditions, recognize Limerick FC's history, acknowledge Treaty United's contribution to senior football in the region, and honour those who have kept the Limerick FC legacy alive.

Ian McMahon, Managing Director of Treaty United, said the new site will help keep supporters and the wider community informed during the transition. "There is a great deal to look forward to as we prepare to play as Limerick FC in 2027, and we want everyone to feel informed and part of that journey," he said.

The microsite also features historic photographs, club news, ticketing details, merchandise links, and partnership opportunities for the 2027 season. These packages span jersey sponsorship, pitch-side advertising, matchday hospitality, academy partnerships, and community initiatives.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362720.localAngle: The website prepares local supporters for the return of Limerick FC and celebrates the region's rich soccer heritage ahead of its 90th anniversary.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362720.originalTitle: Limerick FC prepares for heritage season

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362792.headline: New Limerick power trio Neil Young III to debut at Punch's Blue Bar
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362792.summary: A new Limerick power trio called Neil Young III will mark the Canadian songwriter's 81st birthday with a live gig at Blue Bar, Punch's, on Thursday, November 12. The 9pm show will feature a mix of piano ballads, acoustic favorites, and electric anthems from Young's back catalogue.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362792.story:
Music fans in Limerick can look forward to a new power trio dedicated to the songs of Neil Young, with the band set to make their debut at Blue Bar, Punch’s, on Thursday, November 12. Titled Neil Young III, the group will mark the legendary Canadian songwriter's 81st birthday with a 9pm show spanning piano, acoustic guitar, and a fully cranked Les Paul.

The lineup brings together seasoned local musicians, featuring Mark O’Connor on voice, piano, and guitars, Bryan Healy on bass, and Doug Murray on drums. O'Connor previously played with Tooth and Veneer, Healy performs with 16 Tonnes of Jive and The Groove, and Murray has a background with Woodstar.

Audiences can expect a diverse setlist moving from piano-led numbers like 'Philadelphia' and 'A man needs a maid' to acoustic staples such as 'Harvest moon'. Electric anthems including 'Cinnamon girl' and 'Cortez the killer' will also feature alongside deeper cuts from the 'Ditch Trilogy'.

The band's formation began when Murray suggested a jam session to O'Connor. After realizing O'Connor's vocal and multi-instrumental capabilities, the pair recruited Healy on bass following a chance meeting in Kilkee, cementing the three-piece lineup.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362792.localAngle: The newly formed band, featuring local musicians from the Limerick music scene, will make their debut performance at Blue Bar, Punch's.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362792.originalTitle: Neil Young III – Performing the songs of Neil Young on piano, acoustic and electric guitars.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362781.headline: New Book Recounts Night U2 Played First Official Gig and Won Limerick Competition
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362781.summary: A new book by Brian O'Connell details how U2 played their first official gig and won a £500 prize at the Stella Ballroom during Limerick Civic Week in 1978. The victory helped launch the band's global career despite drawing boos from disgruntled local competitors.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362781.story:
A defining moment in pop music history that took place right here in Limerick is the subject of a new book penned by Brian O'Connell. 'Becoming U2', published on Sunday, November 8, explores the band's origins by focusing on the Pop Group '78 competition staged at the Stella Ballroom during Limerick Civic Week.

The competition, which offered a £500 prize, was the first time Adam Clayton, Larry Mullen, The Edge, and Bono performed together under the name U2. The group had previously gone by Feedback and The Hype before making the trip to Limerick.

The victory was not without controversy. When the Dublin band was announced as the winners, the decision was met with boos as well as cheers from an audience and fellow competitors who believed the novice group could barely play their instruments. Larry Mullen later reflected that the band had no idea how the Limerick win would change their lives.

Three years in the making, the book draws on interviews with eyewitnesses, organisers, and rival musicians who watched U2 take the prize. Endorsed by figures including The Cranberries' Noel Hogan and Adam Clayton himself, the publication captures what author Brian O'Connell describes as a classic 'sliding doors' moment in music history.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362781.localAngle: The book details the pivotal night in 1978 when U2 won a band competition at the Stella Ballroom during Limerick Civic Week, launching their legendary career.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362781.originalTitle: One night in Limerick that launched U2 is the subject of a new book

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53458.headline: Limerick Councillor Backs Patrick O’Donovan Following Ministerial Reassignment
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53458.summary: Fine Gael Councillor Olivia O'Sullivan has voiced her support for Minister Patrick O’Donovan following his temporary ministerial reassignment.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53458.story: Following Monday evening's announcement that Minister Peter Burke will take over functions during Minister O’Donovan’s recovery, fellow Limerick Fine Gael Councillor Olivia O’Sullivan spoke out to wish him well.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53458.localAngle: The story involves Limerick Fine Gael councillors and a local government minister connected to the region.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53458.originalTitle: Limerick councillor speaks out in support of Patrick O’Donovan reassignment

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362804.headline: Shannon Airport secures new twice-weekly Ryanair service to Milan Bergamo for Summer 2027
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362804.summary: Ryanair has announced a new twice-weekly service from Shannon Airport to Milan Bergamo, starting on March 28, 2027. The route will operate on Wednesdays and Sundays, adding an estimated 25,000 seats to the airport's summer programme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362804.story:
Travellers across the Mid-West will have a direct connection to Italy next year following the announcement of a new Ryanair route from Shannon Airport to Milan Bergamo.

Commencing on March 28, 2027, the service will run twice a week on Wednesdays and Sundays. The new route is expected to generate an estimated 25,000 additional seats for the airport's Summer 2027 programme, providing access to Milan, the Italian Lakes, and the wider Lombardy region.

Ray O'Driscoll, CEO of The Shannon Airport Group, described the announcement as a strong vote of confidence in the airport. "Coming on the back of our strongest route programme in 17 years, this new service further strengthens our European network and reinforces Shannon's position as a key gateway for the West of Ireland," he said.

Jade Kirwan, Director of Communications at Ryanair, added that the service offers passengers a direct, low-fare connection to an area renowned for its culture, history, fashion, and food. Tickets for the new route are available to book now via the Ryanair app and website.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362804.localAngle: The new Milan Bergamo service provides passengers across Limerick and the wider Mid-West region with direct access to Italy from Shannon Airport.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362804.originalTitle: New Italian route announced from Shannon Airport

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362753.headline: Limerick business founder trapped with unwanted shares after parting ways with colleagues
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362753.summary: A Limerick business founder seeking to exit a company set up a decade ago has been advised to review shareholder agreements after business partners refused to buy their shares.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362753.story:
A local business owner looking to wash their hands of a company founded with three friends ten years ago has been left with few immediate options after partners refused to buy their stake. The entrepreneur stepped back from day-to-day operations a few years ago when business slowed, though they retained their shares and previously drew a wage alongside the other founders.

Addressing the dilemma in the Limerick Post's Lawlink column, legal experts on Barrington Street advised that the first step is to review the company's constitution and any shareholders' agreement. Such documents typically dictate rules regarding share transfers, rights of first refusal, and valuation mechanisms. In the absence of specific exit provisions, however, founders cannot legally force business partners to buy out a departing shareholder.

While selling to an outside purchaser remains an option, it presents difficulties given the minority stake involved. The guidance notes that while the individual is entitled to resign as a company director and skip general meetings, doing so does not automatically end share ownership or release them from any personal guarantees tied to company borrowings. High Court oppression claims under Section 212 of the Companies Act 2014 are reserved for serious mismanagement and cannot be used simply because a buyer cannot be found.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362753.localAngle: The legal advice column is provided by Alex O'Neill Solicitors based on Barrington Street in Limerick city.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362770.headline: Packed Week of Theatre, Music and Cultural Festivals Kicks Off Across Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362770.summary: Limerick is hosting a busy schedule of events from November 5 to 12, featuring major stage productions at the Lime Tree Theatre, gigs at Dolans, and the ongoing Polish Arts Festival.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362770.story:
A diverse programme of live music, theatre, comedy, and cultural exhibitions is underway across Limerick this week, running from Thursday, November 5, to Thursday, November 12. 

Among the major highlights is the College Players Theatre Company production of Jez Butterworth’s Tony and Olivier Award-winning drama, *The Ferryman*, running at the Lime Tree Theatre. Set in County Armagh in 1981, the play follows the Carney family during their annual harvest feast.

Venues across the city are packed with entertainment, including performances at Dolans—featuring indie-trad trio Project SMOK, local band Maisie’s Room, and former Thin Lizzy frontman Ricky Warwick—alongside screenings and events at the Belltable and Ormston House. 

Cultural offerings also feature prominently this week, including the Polish Arts Festival events such as the theatrical encounter *Un-Masking* at the Belltable, an Ahane Choir recital at St. Patrick’s Church, and the *Samhain: Exploring The Thin Time* exhibition at The People’s Museum of Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362770.localAngle: A diverse lineup of arts, music, and cultural events is taking place across venues throughout Limerick city and county this week.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362770.originalTitle: What’s On in Limerick: Live Music, Theatre, Arts & Events – November 5–12

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362798.headline: Man in 30s hospitalised following stabbing on Limerick city's south side
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362798.summary: Gardaí have launched an investigation after a man sustained stab wounds during an incident at Linden Court on Tuesday evening. The victim was transported to University Hospital Limerick with injuries described as non-life-threatening.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362798.story:
Gardaí are investigating a late-night stabbing incident in Limerick city after a man in his 30s was hospitalised on Tuesday (November 3). Emergency services and Gardaí rushed to Linden Court on the south side of the city shortly before 7:00pm following reports of an alleged assault.

The injured man was treated at the scene before being conveyed to University Hospital Limerick. According to Gardaí, the victim sustained stab wounds during the altercation, but his injuries are not believed to be life-threatening.

Investigating officers are currently working to establish a motive for the attack. A Garda spokesperson confirmed that inquiries remain ongoing as detectives appeal for information regarding the incident on the city's south side.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362798.localAngle: The incident occurred at Linden Court on the south side of Limerick city, prompting a response from local emergency services and University Hospital Limerick.

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53315.headline: Treaty United’s 2026 season ends with 2-0 win ahead of Limerick FC return
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53315.summary: Treaty United closed out their 2026 campaign with a 2-0 victory over Cobh Ramblers at the Markets Field, marking the end of the club's name before Limerick FC returns in 2027.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53315.story:
The final whistle on Treaty United’s 2026 campaign marked the end of an era at the Markets Field on Wednesday, concluding with a 2-0 win over Cobh Ramblers. The match brought the club’s time under the Treaty United name to a close, with Limerick FC set to return to action in 2027.

Treaty finished ninth in the SSE Airtricity Men’s First Division with 42 points, recording 11 wins from their 36 league fixtures. The side struggled for consistency on the road, securing just four away victories, but collected 60 percent of their points at home. Defensively, the team conceded 53 goals across the campaign, though goalkeeper Jack Brady provided stability and kept clean sheets in 25 percent of league fixtures, earning him the Players' Player, Fans' Player, and Blue Army Supporters Club Player of the Season awards.

The season also saw a heavy reliance on younger squad members, with nine players aged 20 or younger featuring regularly as the average squad age shifted marginally to 22.8. Standout young talents included Broadford native Robbie Lynch, who recorded 2,998 minutes and two goals, and 20-year-old Kyle Foley, who made 19 league appearances during a defensive injury crisis. Retaining homegrown talent will be a key challenge for the club moving forward as players gain senior experience.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53315.localAngle: The club's final match at the Markets Field brings an end to the Treaty United identity ahead of Limerick FC's return to the city in 2027.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53315.originalTitle: OPINION: Five things we learned from Treaty United’s 2026 First Division season

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362750.headline: Cllr Pádraigh Reale opposes moving Patrick Sarsfield statue from Cathedral Place
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362750.summary: Labour Councillor Pádraigh Reale has rejected former Mayor John Gilligan's call to relocate the Patrick Sarsfield statue. Reale argues the monument should remain at Cathedral Place while the city focuses on potential efforts to bring Sarsfield's remains back to Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362750.story:
Plans to relocate Limerick's bronze statue of Patrick Sarsfield have faced opposition from Labour Party Councillor Pádraigh Reale, who insists the monument should remain at its current home on Cathedral Place.

The debate follows recent calls from former Limerick Mayor John Gilligan, who suggested that the upcoming regeneration of Bank Place would provide an ideal opportunity to move the sculpture out of relative obscurity and into the spotlight.

However, the City North representative has respectfully disagreed with the proposal. Cllr Reale argued that attention should instead be directed toward acknowledging the community efforts that went into preserving and celebrating the heritage site, including the annual Wild Geese Festival.

Looking ahead, Cllr Reale suggested that local energy should focus on supporting the Sarsfield Homecoming Project and Dr Loïc Guyon in their ongoing efforts to locate and potentially return Sarsfield's remains from Belgium to Limerick for his final resting place.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362750.localAngle: The debate centres on the public placement of a major historic monument dedicated to Limerick hero Patrick Sarsfield within the city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362750.originalTitle: Sarsfield’s statue deserves recognition, not relocation

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362760.headline: Cllr John O'Donoghue calls for public access to Limerick wind-farm noise surveys
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362760.summary: Independent Ireland councillor John O'Donoghue has urged Limerick City and County Council to publish wind-farm noise monitoring reports online or make them available upon request. The local authority rejected the request, citing legal and privacy risks associated with individual household complaints.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362760.story:
Independent Ireland councillor John O'Donoghue has called on Limerick City and County Council to provide public access to completed wind-farm noise surveys and monitoring reports. During the Adare-Rathkeale area meeting, Cllr O'Donoghue asked that these environmental records be published directly on the council's website or made readily available to the public upon request.

In response, council officials informed members that releasing the documents presents legal and privacy risks that distinguish them from standard noise compliance reports. The local authority stated that the surveys and investigation reports directly pertain to individual citizen complaints lodged at specific household locations.

Furthermore, the council cautioned that making complaint-related investigation reports publicly available could interfere with ongoing or potentially pending civil litigation. Officials also noted that open publication of these specific documents risks unfairly singling out individual wind farm operators.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362760.localAngle: The issue was raised at the Adare-Rathkeale area meeting regarding wind-farm noise monitoring within Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362760.originalTitle: Calls for council to provide copies of wind-farm noise surveys

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53467.headline: UL student Tara Cusack trapped by violent nationwide protests in Paris
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53467.summary: University of Limerick student Tara Cusack faced barricades, cancelled in-person classes, and street violence during nationwide protests in France over education and living costs.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53467.story:
University of Limerick student Tara Cusack experienced an unexpected Erasmus semester as widespread protests and riots swept across France, shutting down university campuses and bringing violence to the streets of Paris.

The demonstrations began in mid-September when high school students rallied against staffing shortages, quickly spreading to universities including Cusack's host institution, the Université Paris Cité. Protesters and staff demonstrated over the country's economic climate, overcrowded classrooms, and crumbling infrastructure. Cusack recalled being locked inside her university building during the initial demonstrations, noting that blockades forced all her classes online after three weeks.

Tensions escalated on October 17 during a National Day of Protest called by union parties, which saw mass looting, storefronts ransacked, and police deploying strict curfews and security crackdowns. Cusack avoided the city centre during subsequent large-scale marches, including a major demonstration on October 24, as authorities battled ongoing civil unrest.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53467.localAngle: The story follows a University of Limerick student experiencing unexpected disruption during her studies abroad in Paris.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53467.originalTitle: UL student shares Erasmus experience amid French nationwide protests

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362757.headline: First Choice Financial Services team raises over €2,500 with 2.5m step challenge
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362757.summary: FIRST Choice Financial Services staff completed a team challenge of 2.5 million steps, raising more than €2,500 for Limerick Community Special School and The Aspect Unit SOS Kilkenny.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362757.story:
Staff at FIRST Choice Financial Services have successfully completed a team step challenge, hitting a collective target of 2.5 million steps to raise over €2,500 for two special schools.

The funds will directly benefit the Limerick Community Special School and The Aspect Unit SOS Kilkenny. Both institutions specialise in providing support services and personalised environments tailored to the specific needs, preferences, and sensory profiles of their students.

The money raised from the challenge will be used to support the expansion and capacity of the schools' service provision. In particular, the funds will go toward financing activities and treatments for the children, as well as providing support for the families who rely on the schools' services.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362757.localAngle: The funds raised directly benefit Limerick Community Special School, supporting its local service provision and families in the area.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362757.originalTitle: Over 2.5 million steps clocked up for Limerick school

/node/9324731.headline: Boher Artist Commissioned for BDO Limerick City Office
/node/9324731.summary: A local artist from Boher has been selected by global firm BDO to create a large painting for their Limerick office.
/node/9324731.story: Global accountancy and business advisory firm BDO has commissioned the Boher native to produce a large painting for its Limerick city office.
/node/9324731.localAngle: The commission involves a local artist from Boher creating a major artwork for a business office located in Limerick city.
/node/9324731.originalTitle: Artist awarded commission for BDO Limerick city office

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362812.headline: Whitebox completes construction of new 30,000 sq ft cancer care centre in Moyross
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362812.summary: An 18-month construction project has delivered a new oncology facility at Ballygrennan, marking the first major private-sector investment in the Moyross regeneration area.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362812.story:
Whitebox has officially finished and handed over a new 30,000 sq ft oncology centre at Ballygrennan in Moyross. Completed on time and within budget following an 18-month construction programme, the facility has been transferred to European healthcare real estate firm Aedfica.

Once internal fit-outs are complete, the centre will be operated by CROAL, a joint venture between UPMC and Bon Secours providing cancer-treatment services. The development represents the first significant private investment in the Moyross regeneration area and unlocks the site surrounding the new Coonagh to Knockalisheen Northern Distributor Road scheme.

Martin White, Chief Executive of Whitebox, said the project demonstrates that healthcare infrastructure can be delivered efficiently in the region while boosting vital cancer care services. Further phases are planned for the campus, including a 90-bed nursing home operated by the Mowlam Group, a primary care centre, and 115 new homes built in partnership with Limerick City and County Council and Clúid.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362812.localAngle: The new oncology facility and integrated health campus bring crucial cancer care services and housing infrastructure directly to Limerick and the wider Mid-West.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362812.originalTitle: New cancer care centre opens in Moyross

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362755.headline: UMHL to host annual remembrance service for bereaved families this Sunday
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362755.summary: University Maternity Hospital Limerick will hold its annual remembrance service at the Church of the Holy Rosary on Ennis Road this Sunday, November 8, at 3pm for families grieving the loss of a baby.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362755.story:
University Maternity Hospital Limerick (UMHL) is set to host its annual Remembrance Service this Sunday, November 8, at 3pm. The service will take place at The Church of the Holy Rosary on the Ennis Road.

Organised by the Bereavement and Support team at UMHL, the gathering is held in memory of babies lost through ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage, stillbirth, and neonatal death. Hospital staff will unite with bereaved families to remember babies who have passed away, whether recently or many years ago.

For those who are unable to attend the service in person on the Ennis Road, it will also be streamed live via the parish website's webcam. 

Anyone seeking further information regarding the service can contact the Bereavement and Support team at UMHL directly at 061 483196.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362755.localAngle: The annual service provides a local space for Limerick families and hospital staff to remember babies lost through pregnancy and infancy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362755.originalTitle: Annual Remembrance Service by UMHL this weekend

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53485.headline: UL Student Life Executive Writes Open Letter to Dáil Over Housing Crisis
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53485.summary: The University of Limerick's Student Life Executive has brought the ongoing accommodation crisis directly to national decision-makers through an open letter to Dáil Éireann, media appearances, and protests following their Autumn Student Forum on October 21.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53485.story:
The University of Limerick’s Student Life Executive has escalated its campaign against the student accommodation crisis by writing an open letter to Dáil Éireann. The move followed the executive's Autumn 2026 Student Forum on October 21, where student representatives established their core advocacy aims and held preliminary discussions with UL’s Governing Authority Chancellor regarding housing concerns.

Student Union President Eva McCormack said the executive has taken student grievances directly to national figures. Alongside the letter to the Dáil, representatives lobbied at the Fund Our Future protest and raised the accommodation shortage across national radio and television interviews. McCormack noted that the team has focused heavily on the welfare, financial stability, and personal rights of the student body.

Beyond housing, the executive addressed academic systems by supporting the rollout of the Academic Transformation of Operating Model (ATOM), a project designed to streamline and standardise university operations. The team also reported involvement in broader social advocacy, including demonstrations concerning student fees, LGBTQ+ rights, and Palestinian emancipation, alongside the implementation of an updated Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions list and a preferred name system on campus.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53485.localAngle: The story directly impacts University of Limerick students and the wider Limerick housing and academic community.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53485.originalTitle: UL Student Life Executive writes to Dáil to address housing crisis

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362762.headline: Dr Rachel Mullaly Appointed Consultant Neonatologist at University Maternity Hospital Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362762.summary: HSE Mid West has appointed Dr Rachel Mullaly as a Consultant Neonatologist at University Maternity Hospital Limerick, bringing the regional total to seven specialists. The role will enhance neonatal care following last year's €9.7 million upgrade to the facility's intensive care unit.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362762.story:
University Maternity Hospital Limerick (UMHL) has welcomed Dr Rachel Mullaly as its newest Consultant Neonatologist, bolstering specialist care for newborn babies and their families across the region.

Her appointment brings the total number of consultant neonatologists operating across the Mid West to seven. Dr Mullaly is an active researcher who regularly presents her clinical work at national and international medical meetings.

The appointment follows a major €9.7 million investment in Limerick's neonatal facilities, which saw the completion of a two-storey extension and comprehensive refurbishment at the hospital's Neonatal Intensive Care Unit in 2025.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362762.localAngle: The appointment directly expands specialist newborn healthcare services at University Maternity Hospital Limerick for families across the Mid West region.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362827.headline: Limerick County Council approves Part 8 for new Abbeyfeale graveyard
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362827.summary: Long-running concerns over dwindling burial space in Abbeyfeale have ended as the Council approves plans for a new two-hectare cemetery at Knockbrack, featuring 1,600 plots and a columbarium wall.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362827.story:
Plans for a new two-hectare burial ground in Abbeyfeale have been officially approved by Limerick City and County Council following a special meeting of the Newcastle West Municipal District.

The new graveyard, located at Knockbrack on the outskirts of the West Limerick town near the NCT centre, will feature 1,600 burial plots and a columbarium wall with 350 niches for cremation urns. The development also includes a 200-space car park serving both the burial ground and the existing Greenway, alongside traffic calming measures on the R524.

Elected representatives and local officials welcomed the decision, bringing to a close over a decade of discussions regarding capacity issues at the town's existing Reilig Íde Naofa cemetery on Hill Road. Opened in 1962, the five-acre burial ground has been nearing capacity, prompting local councillors to warn of an impending crisis.

Cathaoirleach of the district, Cllr Liam Galvin, said that extensive trial runs and site selections had finally yielded a solution for the town. The parkland-style development will also incorporate a structured network of pathways, semi-mature tree planting, and an elevated Remembrance Garden aligned visually with the Greenway Hub development.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362827.localAngle: The decision provides a long-awaited solution to a decade-long burial space shortage for families in Abbeyfeale and the wider West Limerick region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362827.originalTitle: Longstanding issue over lack of burial plots at Abbeyfeale cemetery is laid to rest

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362850.headline: Limerick Man in Custody After €72,000 Cocaine and Cash Seizure
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362850.summary: A man in his 40s is being questioned by Gardaí following a raid on the south side of Limerick city on Wednesday that yielded €43,000 in suspected cocaine, nearly €30,000 in cash, and drug paraphernalia.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362850.story:
A Limerick man in his 40s remains in Garda custody following a major drug seizure on the south side of the city on Wednesday. Officers from the Limerick Divisional Drugs Unit, backed by the Armed Support Unit, carried out searches at local residences under a District Court warrant.

During the operation, Gardaí seized approximately €43,000 worth of suspected cocaine along with €29,995 in cash. A vacuum packing machine and other drug-related paraphernalia were also recovered from the properties. The suspected substances have now been sent off for formal analysis.

The detained man is currently being held under Section 2 of the Criminal Justice (Drug Trafficking) Act 1996 at a Garda station in the Limerick area. 

Gardaí confirmed that the operation forms part of Operation Tara, an enhanced national strategy launched in July 2021 aimed at disrupting and dismantling drug trafficking networks at local, national, and international levels. Authorities stated that their investigations into the matter are ongoing.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362850.localAngle: The operation was carried out by local Garda units targeting the sale and supply of drugs on the south side of Limerick city.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362850.originalTitle: Man being questioned after huge cocaine seizure

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362777.headline: Belltable Hosts 10-Year Anniversary Celebration for Narrative 4 on November 13
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362777.summary: O’Connell Street youth organisation Narrative 4 will mark a decade in Ireland with an evening of music, literature, and storytelling at the Belltable. The November 13 event highlights a decade of programmes that have engaged over 100,000 students nationwide.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362777.story:
Award-winning youth organisation Narrative 4 is set to celebrate ten years of operations in Ireland with a special event at the Belltable on Friday, November 13. Titled 'The Power of Stories: Celebrating 10 years of Narrative 4', the evening will feature live music, literature, and storytelling directed by musician and theatre practitioner Ann Blake.

Dr Jennifer McMahon, head of the Department of Psychology at the University of Limerick (UL), will serve as master of ceremonies for the event. Contributions will also come from authors and long-time champions Sarah Moore Fitzgerald and Kerry Neville, alongside collaborations with the Irish World Academy of Music and Dance and UL’s MA in Creative Writing. A key feature of the night will be a live demonstration of the organisation's signature Story Exchange methodology by young people from Limerick.

Established in 2016 at 58 O’Connell Street in the former county library building, Narrative 4 has expanded its reach to work with schools, youth groups, and international partners. Over the past decade, more than 100,000 Irish students have participated in its programmes, while 1,400 teachers across 330 secondary schools have completed its Story Exchange facilitator training.

Co-founder Colum McCann reflected on the milestone, noting that Limerick was chosen for the national headquarters because the city "had a story to tell." The organisation recently secured €250,000 from Creative Ireland to support cross-border initiatives connecting young people in Belfast and Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362777.localAngle: Narrative 4 operates its national headquarters from O'Connell Street in Limerick, engaging young people from across the city and county over the last ten years.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362777.originalTitle: Narrative 4 to mark 10 years in Limerick with evening of words and music at Belltable

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362786.headline: Pianist Yeol Eum Son to Join Irish Chamber Orchestra for UCH Mozart Concert
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362786.summary: Internationally acclaimed pianist Yeol Eum Son will perform two of Mozart's major piano concertos alongside the Irish Chamber Orchestra at the University Concert Hall on Friday, November 20.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362786.story:
Music lovers in Limerick are in for a treat later this month when acclaimed Korean pianist Yeol Eum Son joins the Irish Chamber Orchestra (ICO) for a special concert at the University Concert Hall.

Entitled 'Mozart Illuminated', the Limerick performance takes place on Friday, November 20, at 7.30pm. Directing from the keyboard, Son will integrate directly with the orchestra—which is based at the University of Limerick—to listen, respond, and shape the music alongside the players.

The programme begins with Mozart’s Divertimento in D major, K.136, composed when he was just 16. It will be followed by the dramatic Piano Concerto No. 24 in C minor, K.491, and the radiant Piano Concerto No. 21 in C major, K.467, whose famous slow movement was featured in the film Elvira Madigan.

Tickets for the University Concert Hall performance are priced at €30, €25, €10, and €5. The orchestra and soloist will also take the programme to Dublin's Whyte Recital Hall on November 19 and St Michael’s Catholic Church in Blackrock, Cork, on November 21. Further information is available via the Irish Chamber Orchestra website.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362786.localAngle: The concert takes place at the University Concert Hall, featuring the University of Limerick-based Irish Chamber Orchestra.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362786.originalTitle: Yeol Eum Son brings Mozart’s brilliance to UCH with ICO

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53462.headline: Twelve Limerick schools approved for funding under €80m national climate scheme
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53462.summary: Minister for Education and Youth Hildegarde Naughton has announced that 12 schools across Limerick will receive funding under the 2027 Climate Action Summer Works Scheme to improve energy efficiency and building conditions.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53462.story:
Twelve schools across Limerick have been greenlit to receive funding under the 2027 Climate Action Summer Works Scheme, part of an €80 million national investment announced by Minister for Education and Youth Hildegarde Naughton. 

The scheme aims to help schools carry out small and medium-scale building upgrades during the summer holiday period. Projects are assessed based on individual school needs and the urgency of the works required, with a particular focus this year on supporting special schools.

The 12 Limerick institutions approved for the funding are Limerick Community Special School, Desmond College, Scoil Naomh Muire, Eas Géitine, Thomond Primary School, Limerick City East Educate Together NS, St Joseph's, St Brigid's NS, S N Gleann Gcreabhar, S N Naomh Padraig, St James' NS, St John's Convent, and S N Sheanain.

Funding will allow schools to undertake works such as insulation upgrades, LED lighting installation, EV charger provision, and bike rack facilities to support active travel. Minister Naughton noted that the multi-annual approach means schools not approved in this initial round remain eligible for future consideration.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53462.localAngle: Twelve local schools across Limerick have been approved for funding to upgrade their buildings and improve energy efficiency.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53462.originalTitle: 12 Limerick projects greenlit for €80 million climate scheme

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362822.headline: Maurice Quinlivan Demands HSE Secure Private Beds to Ease UHL Overcrowding
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362822.summary: Limerick Sinn Féin TD Maurice Quinlivan has called on the Minister for Health to urgently secure private hospital beds in the Mid-West to tackle severe overcrowding at University Hospital Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362822.story:
Limerick Sinn Féin TD Maurice Quinlivan has urged the Minister for Health to instruct the HSE to urgently identify and secure available private hospital beds in Limerick and the wider Mid-West region. The call comes as University Hospital Limerick (UHL) continues to record some of the highest levels of overcrowding in the State, with more than 19,000 people treated on trolleys so far this year.

Mr Quinlivan said that while private beds alone will not resolve the long-standing capacity issues at UHL, immediate action is necessary as the region approaches the winter months. He suggested that purchasing beds or entering contractual arrangements with private healthcare providers could secure vital inpatient, rehabilitation, and step-down beds to help transfer appropriate patients and ease pressure on the emergency department.

“The people of Limerick and the wider Mid-West cannot continue to hear promises while this situation persists,” Mr Quinlivan said. He added that the region has been underfunded for decades by successive governments, leaving patients, families, and hardworking healthcare staff exposed to sustained and unfair pressure.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362822.localAngle: The story directly addresses chronic overcrowding and healthcare capacity issues at University Hospital Limerick, impacting patients and staff across Limerick and the Mid-West.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362822.originalTitle: Quinlivan calls for use of private beds to stem overcrowding

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362832.headline: Limerick pharmacies secure finalist spots in Irish Pharmacy Excellence Awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362832.summary: Several Limerick pharmacies, including branches in Dooradoyle, have reached the final stage of the Irish Pharmacy Excellence Awards 2026 following a competitive selection process involving over 250 entries.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362832.story:
A number of pharmacies across Limerick have been named as finalists for the Irish Pharmacy Excellence Awards 2026. The shortlist was announced following a high volume of entries, with more than 250 submissions received across the various categories.

Among the nominees are CarePlus Pharmacies located in Dooradoyle and other areas throughout the county. The national awards program is designed to acknowledge the work carried out by pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, pharmacy assistants, and wider teams operating within community pharmacies, hospitals, and other healthcare settings across the Republic of Ireland.

Following the announcement of the finalists, the overall winners will be revealed later this month. A black-tie ceremony is scheduled to take place at the Dublin Royal Convention Centre on Saturday, November 21, 2026, where the successful candidates across all categories will be officially announced.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362832.localAngle: Local pharmacies across Limerick have been shortlisted for national recognition at the upcoming Irish Pharmacy Excellence Awards.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362832.originalTitle: Limerick pharmacies recognised at national awards

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362830.headline: Rathbane Road Speed Survey Scheduled to Inform Traffic Calming Measures
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362830.summary: Limerick City and County Council has confirmed a traffic speed survey in Rathbane following queries from Cllr Catherine Slattery, with results expected to determine future road safety measures.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362830.story:
A road speed survey in Rathbane is set to pave the way for potential traffic calming measures in the area, following a query from Fianna Fáil councillor Catherine Slattery at this month's Metropolitan District meeting.

In response to Cllr Slattery, the Council revealed that the traffic speed survey is scheduled to be completed in late October 2026. The findings will then be assessed to establish whether traffic calming or other road safety interventions are required at the location.

Subject to the results of the survey, the local authority will develop appropriate design proposals and explore funding opportunities to implement any necessary measures in line with the Council's Traffic Calming Policy.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362830.localAngle: The proposed survey addresses local road safety concerns raised by a public representative for the Limerick Metropolitan District.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362830.originalTitle: Proposed road speed survey considered for Rathbane

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362871.headline: Banríon to play live in-store set at Steamboat Music this Saturday
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362871.summary: Indie-rock project banríon will perform live at Steamboat Music this Saturday, November 7, at 3pm to celebrate the release of her debut album, 'untarnishing'. Róisín Ní Haicéid recently relocated to Limerick, drawing inspiration from the city's independent music scene.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362871.story:
Indie-rock artist Róisín Ní Haicéid, performing under the moniker banríon, is set to play a live in-store set at Steamboat Music this Saturday, November 7, at 3pm. The performance marks the release of her debut nine-track album, 'untarnishing'.

Ní Haicéid recently relocated to Limerick, a move directly inspired by her experiences attending Féile na Gréine since 2022. She is already building a new band in the city and has rehearsals underway. "The DIY scene here is amazing, and there are so many talented musicians, but there’s also this ethos of helping each other out and supporting each other that I think is really special," she said.

The debut album captures her musical journey from 2022 to 2024 and explores themes of love, loss, belonging, and self-forgiveness. It follows her earlier work with two EPs and support slots for bands such as NewDad, Lime Garden, and Pillow Queens, alongside a 2023 appearance on the TG4 series Buille, which was filmed in Dolans.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362871.localAngle: The artist recently relocated to Limerick after being drawn to the city's independent music scene through her involvement with Féile na Gréine.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362871.originalTitle: Banríon to play instore at Steamboat Music this Saturday to mark release of her debut album

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362857.headline: Limerick's Kilmartin Educational Services wins two national Lean business awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362857.summary: Kilmartin Educational Services has won Micro Lean Business of the Year and the Sustainability Award at the Lean Business Ireland Excellence Awards in County Meath.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362857.story:
Limerick-based Kilmartin Educational Services is celebrating a double win after picking up two accolades at the Lean Business Ireland Excellence Awards held at the Johnstown Estate in County Meath on Thursday, 22 October.

The local educational provider took home both the Micro Lean Business of the Year Award and the Sustainability Award. The annual event brings together organisations from across Ireland to recognise excellence in continuous improvement, operational efficiency, innovation, and sustainability, with other notable participants including Tirlán and Europcar.

Principal Julie Kilmartin expressed delight at the double win, noting that the business has always focused on identifying areas for improvement and finding better ways of working. "Our focus remains on providing high-quality educational support while making our business as efficient and sustainable as possible," she said.

Based in Limerick, Kilmartin Educational Services offers tuition, supervised study, examination preparation, and study skills development, alongside online learning services that extend its reach beyond the local area. The awards highlight the integration of Lean principles and environmental practices into the company's daily operations.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362857.localAngle: The award-winning educational services provider is based in Limerick, offering local tuition, supervised study, and exam preparation.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362857.originalTitle: Kilmartin Educational Services Celebrates Double Win at National Business Awards

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53490.headline: Moyross Man Arrested as Missing Person Probe Becomes Murder Investigation
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53490.summary: A 35-year-old man remains in custody in Northern Ireland following his arrest over the suspected murder of missing Limerick mother-of-four Carrie Mullane. The 39-year-old was last seen travelling to Enniskillen on October 10.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53490.story:
A 35-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of the murder of Carrie Mullane, a 39-year-old mother of four from Moyross who was reported missing nearly four weeks ago. Detectives questioning the suspect were granted an additional 36 hours by a court to continue their inquiries.

Ms Mullane was last seen on October 10 while travelling to Enniskillen, County Fermanagh. Police in Northern Ireland confirmed the arrest following a shift in the investigation from a missing-person case to a suspected murder inquiry. Detective Superintendent Richard Thornton from the PSNI’s Serious Crime Branch noted that her disappearance was "extremely out of character," as she was accustomed to being in daily contact with family and friends.

Muddying the tragedy for her relatives, Ms Mullane's sister Sandra travelled to Northern Ireland to liaise with police, while her son Jayden shared a public plea online. The Moyross community rallied around the family on Tuesday evening, November 3, holding a vigil to show solidarity.

Gardaí are appealing to anyone with CCTV or dashcam footage from the Wellington Road or Trasna Park areas between 8.30pm and 10pm on October 10 to contact emergency services on 999 or 112.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53490.localAngle: The victim is a mother of four from Moyross whose disappearance and suspected murder has deeply impacted the local Limerick community.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53490.originalTitle: BREAKING: Man arrested on suspicion of Moyross murder

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362834.headline: Culture Minister Patrick O’Donovan launches Pat McLoughlin's new novel in Newcastle West
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362834.summary: County Limerick author Pat McLoughlin has launched his new crime novel, Retribution – When Justice is Not Enough, at the Longcourt House Hotel. All profits from the book will be donated to Friends of St Ita’s Hospital.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362834.story:
County Limerick author Pat McLoughlin launched his latest novel to a packed house at the Longcourt House Hotel in Newcastle West. Minister for Culture Patrick O’Donovan officially launched the book at the well-attended local event.

Titled Retribution – When Justice is Not Enough, the new novel explores the themes of crime and punishment in Ireland. The launch event featured a dynamic reading of the book’s opening chapter delivered by actor Johnny Corkery.

All profits generated from the sale of the new novel will be donated directly to Friends of St Ita’s Hospital in Newcastle West.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362834.localAngle: The book was launched in Newcastle West by local TD and Culture Minister Patrick O’Donovan, with all proceeds benefiting Friends of St Ita’s Hospital.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362834.originalTitle: New novel from Limerick author launched

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53495.headline: UL Student and Metal Band Misery Goblin Release Third Single
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53495.summary: First-year UL journalism student Danny Lysaght has released a new heavy metal single titled 'Crossroads of Time' with their band Misery Goblin, alongside plans for future demo recordings and studio work.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53495.story:
A first-year Journalism and Digital Communications student at the University of Limerick has released their third studio single with local heavy metal band Misery Goblin.

Fronted by vocalist Danny Lysaght alongside bandmates Luke O’Donovan on guitar, Ollie McFall on bass, and Lucy Fitzgibbon on drums, the group dropped their latest track, 'Crossroads of Time,' across all streaming platforms accompanied by a music video. The single was produced by Anthony Monahan and Richard Dowling. Since settling into their current lineup and sound in February 2026, Lysaght says the band has moved away from sprawling, ten-minute tracks like 2025's 'Tentacles of Doom' in favor of snappier death metal arrangements. “The main thing that I’ve taken to heart is the importance of conciseness in writing,” Lysaght said, noting how their UL studies have influenced the band's tighter new material.

Following the release, Misery Goblin plans to record an album of raw demo tracks during rehearsal sessions to capture their live sound, alongside upcoming studio sessions to record earlier material from the band's formative era. The group also expects to return to live performances soon.

In addition to fronting the band, Lysaght recently released a solo album titled 'Gelatinous Chemical Sludge' under the moniker QBL, exploring a musical vision free from genre constraints.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53495.localAngle: The band features local Limerick musicians, with the frontman studying journalism at the University of Limerick.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53495.originalTitle: UL Journalism student to release third single with metal band

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53556.headline: Bomb threats force nationwide evacuations at RTÉ, Newstalk and Irish Independent offices
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53556.summary: Major media organisations across Ireland, including RTÉ and Newstalk, were evacuated on Friday morning following threatening emails. Broadcasting was temporarily disrupted as emergency services responded to the security alerts.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53556.story:
Staff at several media organisations across Ireland were forced to evacuate their premises on Friday morning, November 6, following a series of bomb threats. RTÉ's Donnybrook campus in Dublin was among the locations cleared after the national broadcaster received a threatening email shortly before 9am.

The security alert caused immediate disruption to normal broadcasting schedules, with RTÉ switching to pre-recorded programmes as a precautionary measure. In a statement, the broadcaster confirmed that staff safety remains its priority and that normal services would resume as soon as possible in consultation with the Gardaí.

Other prominent media offices affected included Marconi House—which hosts Newstalk, Today FM, and other Bauer Media stations—as well as the Dublin premises of The Irish Independent. An Garda Síochána confirmed it is aware of threats made against media organisations both in Ireland and across Europe.

The nationwide evacuations follow a wave of similar security alerts involving bomb threats against European airlines in recent days, which disrupted at least 27 flights on Thursday, November 5. Authorities have not yet independently established the identity of those responsible or whether the incidents are connected. Investigations into the ongoing security alerts remain active.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53556.localAngle: While the physical evacuations took place in Dublin, the disruption directly impacted national news and broadcasting services relied upon by audiences across Limerick.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53556.originalTitle: BREAKING: RTÉ buildings evacuated following bomb threat

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362860.headline: Teen sent to Circuit Court over violent Shannon assaults and off-licence attack
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362860.summary: A teenager accused of two brutal assaults in Shannon, including photographing a victim on the ground before stamping on his head, has been sent forward to the Circuit Court after a judge declined jurisdiction at Ennis Children's Court.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362860.story:
A 17-year-old youth has been sent forward for trial to Ennis Circuit Court after a judge declined jurisdiction in a case involving multiple violent incidents in Shannon, including an attack where a victim was photographed on the ground before being stamped on.

Det Garda Paul Coleman told the Children’s Court in Ennis that the teenager was "front and centre" in the alleged assaults of two men at Brú na Sionna on October 26, 2025. The court heard evidence that the level of violence used was considerable, detailing how one victim was dragged from grass to a pavement before being repeatedly stamped on and struck in the face. Det Garda Coleman stated that the accused took a photograph of one injured party with his phone while he lay on the ground before stamping on his head once more. Both victims were described as intoxicated and unable to defend themselves.

In a separate incident on May 5, 2025, Garda Colette Acton outlined allegations that the then-16-year-old assaulted the owner of the Carry Out off-licence at Drumgeely. The owner had given chase after the teenager allegedly stole a pack of Bulmers. Garda Acton said the accused attempted to bite the owner on the face, pulled him down by the head, bit his back, and struck him three times with a hurley, leaving the victim with injuries requiring a tetanus injection.

Solicitor Stiofán Fitzpatrick told the court that his client was in the throes of addiction at the time of the offenses. However, Det Garda Coleman noted that CCTV footage showed the accused did not appear impaired during the assaults. Mr Fitzpatrick added that his client is now in gainful employment and has not come to the attention of Gardaí since.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362860.localAngle: The court proceedings concern serious criminal charges originating from neighboring County Clare, a frequent area of legal and commuter crossover for the greater Limerick region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362860.originalTitle: Teen accused of assault took photo of alleged victim on the ground

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53529.headline: Bon Secours Group Reports €503.9m Revenue Driven by Limerick Hospital Growth
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53529.summary: Newly filed accounts reveal a €25.1m revenue increase for the Bon Secours health network, following a surge in inpatient and outpatient activity at its facilities, including the recently opened Limerick hospital.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53529.story:
The Bon Secours private health network has reported group-wide revenues of €503.9m, marking a €25.1m increase driven by a significant rise in both inpatient and outpatient activity.

Directors at the hospital network pointed to the growth in patient numbers across the group as the primary driver behind the financial figures. The revenue milestone follows a period of heavy investment and construction, which previously saw the group report pre-tax losses of €4.77m in 2024 following a €20.45m deficit the year prior. Company directors noted that these earlier deficits were compounded by high mobilisation costs—including staffing, administration, and training—alongside a €4.1m impairment charge from IT asset write-downs and administrative costs.

The 170-bed facility in Ballysimon, Castletroy, opened its doors in September 2025 after being constructed in just under 26 months. Representing the first acute hospital built in Ireland in nearly two decades, the €503.9m network now employs over 700 staff locally, complementing the provider's existing footprint in Limerick City Centre alongside operations in Cork, Galway, Dublin, and Tralee.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53529.localAngle: The €170-bed facility in Ballysimon, Castletroy, has brought over 700 jobs to the Midwest as the first acute hospital built in Ireland in nearly two decades.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53529.originalTitle: Limerick hospital sees €503.9m in revenue to Bon Secours group

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362795.headline: Authors Sharon Guard and June O’Sullivan to talk writing at O’Mahony’s
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362795.summary: Local novelists Sharon Guard and June O’Sullivan will discuss the realities of writing and publishing with Eoin Devereux at O’Mahony’s Booksellers on November 19.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362795.story:
Two novelists with strong Limerick connections are set to share insights into the creative writing process during a public event at O’Mahony’s Booksellers this month. Sharon Guard and June O’Sullivan will join Limerick writer Eoin Devereux for 'Becoming A Creative Writer' on Thursday, November 19.

The event at the O’Connell Street bookstore will explore the day-to-day realities of drafting a novel, navigating the agent process, and securing publication. Both authors are graduates of the University of Limerick’s Masters in Creative Writing programme and will read from their latest works during the evening.

June O’Sullivan, who was born in County Limerick, authored the recent novel *The Sky Is Not Enough*, which explores the life of pioneering aviator Sophie Pierce. Meanwhile, Sharon Guard’s latest release, *The Silence of October*, features a protagonist hailing from Janesboro.

The discussion begins at 7pm. Organisers have advised that early booking through Eventbrite is recommended for those wishing to attend.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362795.localAngle: The event features Limerick-linked authors discussing their work at a landmark city centre bookstore and highlights graduates of UL's Creative Writing programme.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362795.originalTitle: Novelists Sharon Guard and June O’Sullivan to discuss life as a writer at O’Mahony’s

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362856.headline: UL study reveals female-presenting AI assistants are paid 10% less than male counterparts
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362856.summary: New research from the University of Limerick shows that human gender bias extends to artificial intelligence, with participants paying female-presenting AI agents 10.25 per cent less than male-presenting ones for identical work.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362856.story:
Researchers at the University of Limerick (UL) have found that human gender biases in the workplace are being replicated in interactions with artificial intelligence. The study, co-authored by Dr Mary Hausfield of UL’s Kemmy Business School, examined whether the gender pay gap extends to AI systems.

As part of the study, 189 workers were placed in a virtual reality office to complete tasks with human-like AI assistants featuring either a male or female appearance. Participants were then given real money to divide between themselves and the AI assistant for the completed work. Despite utilizing the exact same underlying technology and capabilities, the female-presenting AI agent, named 'Johanna', was paid 10.25 per cent less than the male-presenting agent, 'Johan'. Additionally, Johan was perceived as more human-like by the participants.

Dr Hausfield noted that the findings challenge the assumption that artificial intelligence is entirely neutral. She warned that the way systems are designed and presented can activate existing human biases.

"As AI agents become more common in the workplace, we need to think carefully about the characteristics we give them and the behaviours those choices may encourage," Dr Hausfield said. "We don’t want to inadvertently reproduce existing inequalities in a new technological setting."
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362856.localAngle: The research was conducted by academics at the University of Limerick's Kemmy Business School.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362856.originalTitle: UL research asks if gender pay gap extends to AI

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362884.headline: Wasps vs Humans to play free lunchtime gig at Steamboat Records
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362884.summary: Electronic punk-folk duo Wasps vs Humans will perform a free in-store set at Steamboat Music this Saturday, November 7, at 1pm, ahead of their official album launch later this month.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362884.story:
Music fans in Limerick will have the chance to see Wasps vs Humans up close this Saturday, November 7, when the duo takes to the floor at Steamboat Music for a free lunchtime set at 1pm. 

The performance comes ahead of the band’s official album launch for their second release, *The Day Homo Sapiens Destroyed the Earth*. Produced in partnership with Anthem Vinyl, the record marks the duo's first vinyl pressing and recently earned a four-star review from The Irish Times, which praised its abrasive punk-folk sound.

Formed by punk poet and drummer Carl Antony Plover alongside musician wife Linda Plover, the band combines drums, bodhrán, whistles, and electronic beats to tackle themes of inner-city crime and social decay. 

Saturday's in-store appearance serves as a warm-up before the band returns to Limerick on Friday, November 20, for their official album launch at The Record Room, located within The Commercial, featuring special guests Japanese Jesus.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362884.localAngle: The event takes place at Steamboat Music in Limerick, ahead of the band's upcoming album launch at The Record Room.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362884.originalTitle: Wasps vs Humans to play free in-store set at Steamboat Records

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362928.headline: George’s Quay Clinic Becomes First in Ireland to Launch Visagé Define Pro
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362928.summary: Ultimate Health Clinic in Limerick is marking the nationwide debut of the Visagé Define Pro treatment by offering free 15-minute trials and 20% off for its first 20 clients.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362928.story:
