Ultimate Health Clinic on George’s Quay has become the first clinic in Ireland to introduce the Visagé Define Pro treatment. To celebrate the launch, the Limerick facility is offering free 15-minute trial sessions alongside a 20 per cent discount for the first 20 clients, giving locals an opportunity to experience the procedure and discuss their personal wellness goals with the team.

The non-invasive treatment combines electromagnetic muscle stimulation with radiofrequency technology, designed to support muscle conditioning and improve skin firmness. While electromagnetic pulses trigger repeated muscle contractions, the warmth from the radiofrequency is intended to aid collagen production. Target areas for the procedure include the abdomen, glutes, thighs, and arms, subject to an individual assessment of suitability.

Clinic representatives noted that maintaining muscle mass and skin firmness can be a particular concern for individuals experiencing changes in body shape following weight loss. A personalised assessment is emphasized, and a course of treatments may be recommended depending on each client's specific goals. The complimentary trials are intended to provide an opportunity for clients to ask questions and determine if the treatment suits their needs before committing to further sessions. Interested individuals can contact the clinic directly at 061 315785.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362928.localAngle: The nationwide debut of the Visagé Define Pro treatment is taking place exclusively at the Ultimate Health Clinic on George’s Quay in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362928.originalTitle: Ultimate Health Clinic introduces Visagé Define Pro with free trials

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362862.headline: Works on long-awaited Clarina bus shelter to begin shortly
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362862.summary: Construction on a new bus shelter in Clarina is set to begin in the coming days following the finalisation of a land agreement.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362862.story:
Construction work on a new bus shelter in Clarina is expected to get underway in the coming days after a crucial land agreement was finalised.

Fine Gael councillor Dan McSweeney confirmed that the project can now progress following successful negotiations with a local landowner. Cllr McSweeney thanked the landowner for their positive engagement, stating that it helped make the infrastructure project a reality.

"The local community has waited far too long for this simple piece of essential infrastructure," Cllr McSweeney said, adding that he is pleased to see the project finally moving forward.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362862.localAngle: The new bus shelter provides essential transport infrastructure for commuters in the Clarina area of County Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362862.originalTitle: Works to commence on long-awaited bus shelter in Clarina

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362919.headline: Clúid opens applications for 12 new cost-rental apartments in Knockhill
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362919.summary: Applications are now open for 12 two-bedroom cost-rental apartments in Knockhill, Co Limerick, with rents set at €1,594 per month. The A-rated homes are priced at least 25 per cent below the local market average.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362919.story:
Applications officially opened on Wednesday, November 4, for 12 brand new, A-rated two-bedroom apartments in the Amharc Abhann development located in the Knockhill suburb. Delivered by housing association Clúid, the properties are being offered at €1,594 per month, sitting at least 25 per cent below the average market rent for the area.

Alongside the reduced rates, successful applicants will secure life-long tenancies with responsive management and maintenance support. The development is situated close to local amenities including schools, shops, and health centres, and benefits from regular bus connections into Limerick city centre.

Clúid CEO Averil Power noted that high demand is expected due to the location, build quality, and reduced rents. Interested applicants must complete their submissions online via the Clúid website before 5pm on Wednesday, November 18, to be included in the allocation lottery.

The Knockhill scheme was delivered by Clúid in partnership with Limerick City and County Council, with support from the Department of Housing, Heritage and Local Government, The Housing Agency, and the Housing Finance Agency. Formation Homes served as the developer, while Occu is partnering on the allocation and onboarding process.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362919.localAngle: The development provides secure, below-market housing options for households in the Limerick area close to local amenities and the city centre.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362915.headline: Minister Patrick O'Donovan hospitalized at UHL following illness at home
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362915.summary: Cabinet Minister Patrick O'Donovan has been admitted to the high dependency unit at University Hospital Limerick after falling ill at his home on Thursday night. It is the second time in less than a month that the Limerick TD has been rushed to the hospital following medical emergencies related to his epilepsy diagnosis.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362915.story:
Minister for Communications, Media, Arts, Culture and Sport Patrick O'Donovan was rushed to University Hospital Limerick (UHL) on Thursday night after falling ill at his home. The 49-year-old Fine Gael TD is currently being treated in the hospital's high dependency unit.

This marks the second time in less than a month that the Limerick politician has been admitted to UHL following a medical emergency. On October 13, he was rushed to the hospital's Intensive Care Unit after taking seriously ill while hosting a meeting of European Union Telecommunications Ministers at the University of Limerick. Following that incident, Enterprise Minister Peter Burke took over Mr O'Donovan's ministerial duties on a temporary basis.

Mr O'Donovan has previously spoken publicly about his diagnosis of deep frontal lobe epilepsy, which was confirmed after he collapsed in the Dáil in June 2023. He has shared that he initially kept the condition private before deciding to speak openly about his health.

Earlier this week, local representatives in the Newcastle West Municipal District agreed to send a letter of support to the Minister. Meanwhile, his department has stated that any return to work will be guided strictly by medical advice.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362915.localAngle: The Limerick TD and former local councillor has been receiving ongoing treatment at University Hospital Limerick following medical emergencies in the county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362915.originalTitle: Minister Patrick O’Donovan back in hospital

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362864.headline: Abbeyfeale welcomes new N21 link road and 21 parking spaces on former bar site
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362864.summary: A new link road connecting the N21 National Road to the Grove Crescent car park in Abbeyfeale has been completed. The project also delivers 21 new on-street parking spaces on the former site of O'Riordan's Bar.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362864.story:
A new link road connecting the N21 National Road directly to the Grove Crescent car park in Abbeyfeale has officially been completed. 

The infrastructure project marks a significant milestone in the delivery of the Abbeyfeale Traffic Management Plan and the town's wider public realm enhancement programme. Alongside the new roadway, the development provides 21 new on-street parking spaces for motorists.

The project has completely transformed the site, which was formerly occupied by O’Riordan’s Bar, into an integral piece of town centre infrastructure. Local motorists and pedestrians can now benefit from improved access, parking, connectivity, and traffic circulation throughout the town centre.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362864.localAngle: The project directly improves traffic flow and parking infrastructure in the West Limerick town of Abbeyfeale.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362864.originalTitle: New link road in Abbeyfeale completed

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53570.headline: Mayor John Moran signs contracts to transform Wickham Street site into pocket park
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53570.summary: Limerick has taken control of properties at 20-24 Wickham Street to develop a new city centre pocket park. The abandoned garden site will be redesigned with a local 'Pig town' theme.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53570.story:
Contracts were signed on Friday giving the city control of properties numbered 20 to 24 on Wickham Street, paving the way for a new pocket park in the heart of Limerick. 

The site was previously an abandoned, fenced-off garden. After a previous development proposal fell through, the Mayor’s Office used mayoral funds to acquire the properties and transfer them to Limerick City for redevelopment following a clean-up operation over the past year.

Mayor of Limerick John Moran told the Limerick Voice that the new park will celebrate the area's heritage. “Our garden team have come up with a really cool design for people to just hang out in this area, and it’s all about the idea of Limerick being pig town and so the theme of the whole garden is actually all about pig town,” he said.

The pocket park is designed to sit within Limerick's historical zone—historically home to four bacon factories—with the aim of boosting social life in an economically important part of the city centre.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53570.localAngle: The acquisition of derelict city centre land directly impacts urban regeneration and public spaces in Limerick.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53570.originalTitle: Mayor secures Wickham street site for new pocket park

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362888.headline: Xeinadin announces 70 graduate roles with positions open in Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362888.summary: Accountancy firm Xeinadin is recruiting 70 graduates for its 2027 early careers programme, marking a 40 per cent increase in intake with opportunities available in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362888.story:
Limerick graduates are set to benefit from a major recruitment drive as business advisory firm Xeinadin rolls out its 2027 early careers programme. The company has announced plans to take on 70 graduates, representing a 40 per cent increase from last year's intake.

The expansion comes as emerging technologies like AI change working practices across the accountancy sector. Xeinadin operates 33 offices across Ireland, with the graduate positions available across its regional network as well as major cities.

Sandra Clarke, Managing Partner for Ireland at Xeinadin, said that while AI and other emerging technologies are creating efficiencies, they will not replace the need for graduates. "Our work with SMEs is highly relationship-driven. Clients want access to people; they want to meet and hear from people," she said. "We want to be at the forefront of developing those people skills and inspiring the next generation of business advisors in Ireland."

Successful applicants will gain practical experience across accounting, tax, bookkeeping, and audit during their first one to two years. Graduates typically gain exposure to a range of sectors and clients within Xeinadin's core SME market.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362888.localAngle: The recruitment drive offers new employment and career development opportunities for graduates based in Limerick through Xeinadin's regional office network.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362888.originalTitle: Grads benefit from expansion of programme

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53567.headline: Keenan scores hat-trick as Ireland defeat Argentina 42-12 on home soil
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53567.summary: Hugo Keenan scored a hat-trick and Limerick's Craig Casey started at scrum-half as Ireland secured a 42-12 bonus-point victory over Argentina on Friday. The win moves Andy Farrell's side to the top of the Northern Hemisphere table.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53567.story:
Hugo Keenan sealed a man-of-the-match performance with a well-deserved hat-trick as Ireland extended their unbeaten home run against Argentina to 12 games with a 42-12 bonus-point victory at the Aviva Stadium on Friday night.

Limerick's Craig Casey featured in the starting XV at scrum-half, playing his part as Andy Farrell's side moved to the top of the Northern Hemisphere table. Sam Prendergast also starred with a 100% success rate from five conversions, alongside scoring his first senior international try following a 40-metre break through the Argentinian defence. Captain Dan Sheehan and Rónan Kelleher added further tries to complete the dominant scoreline.

Los Pumas struggled to contain the hosts, not helped by yellow cards shown to Justo Piccardo and Efrain Elias during the encounter. The result leaves Ireland with a clean sweep of wins against the South American side on home soil.

Looking ahead, the Ireland squad will return to the Aviva Stadium next week to face Fiji in their fifth match of the Nations Championship.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53567.localAngle: Shannon RFC's Craig Casey started at scrum-half for Ireland in the bonus-point victory over Argentina.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53567.originalTitle: Hugo Keenan hat-trick seals Ireland bonus-point win over Argentina

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362931.headline: Jury Sent Home for Weekend After Five Hours in Josie Ray Murder Trial
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362931.summary: The Central Criminal Court jury deliberating on the murder trial of 52-year-old Hasan Ali Gori has been sent home for the weekend without reaching a verdict after nearly five hours of discussions.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362931.story:
The jury in the trial of Hasan Ali Gori, accused of murdering 89-year-old great-grandmother Josephine “Josie” Ray, was sent home for the weekend after deliberating for a total of four hours and 46 minutes. The panel retired last Wednesday following three weeks of evidence at the Central Criminal Court, but did not sit on Thursday.

Mr Gori, a 52-year-old Chad native, has pleaded not guilty to the murder of Ms Ray, whose body was discovered in her home at St Joseph’s Park, Nenagh, County Tipperary, on August 4, 2024. State pathologist Dr Yvonne McCartney testified that the victim died of strangulation and smothering, having sustained two broken bones in her neck and 44 bruises across her body.

During closing arguments, senior prosecuting counsel Lorcan Connolly told the jury that Ms Ray had tried to "fight off" her attacker, pointing to defensive bruises on her forearms and the presence of Mr Gori's DNA under her fingernails. The prosecution argued that the accused had motive and opportunity, suggesting he was at risk of eviction and losing social welfare payments tied to the household.

Defence counsel Aidan Doyle countered by highlighting earlier testimony regarding family tensions and disputes at the property prior to the incident. The jury will resume its deliberations when the trial recommences.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362931.localAngle: The high-profile murder trial is being heard at the Central Criminal Court sitting in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362931.originalTitle: Jury sent home for weekend in Josie Ray trial

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362893.headline: Elisa O'Donovan calls for extended winter opening hours in Limerick parks
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362893.summary: Social Democrats Councillor Elisa O'Donovan has urged Limerick City and County Council to keep public parks open later during winter. The local authority cited staffing, security, and capital investment costs in response.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362893.story:
Social Democrats Councillor Elisa O'Donovan has called on Limerick City and County Council to extend winter opening hours across public parks in the city, particularly those featuring sports and recreational facilities.

During this month’s Metropolitan District meeting, Cllr O'Donovan also asked the local authority to consider improving lighting in parks where required. She argued that better illumination would allow for greater and safer use of the public spaces during dark winter evenings.

In response to the proposal, the Council explained that extending opening hours later into the evening would require additional operational resources. This would include revised working hours for Park Rangers, increased staffing requirements, and potentially higher security costs for opening and closing the facilities.

Regarding the request for improved lighting, the Council stated that such a measure would require significant capital investment, alongside ongoing maintenance and energy costs.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362893.localAngle: The proposal affects public parks and recreational facilities managed by Limerick City and County Council across the 061 area.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362893.originalTitle: Calls for extended winter opening hours across public parks

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362925.headline: Limerick Celtics and Eagles Face Crucial Men's and Women's National Cup Clashes
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362925.summary: Limerick Celtics host Tralee Warriors in the Men's National Cup at Crescent College this Sunday, while Limerick Eagles travel to holders Killester on Saturday.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362925.story:
Limerick Celtics entertain Tralee Warriors in the opening round of the Men’s National Cup at Crescent College this Sunday at 3.15pm. Celtics currently sit atop the Super League with only one loss in their opening six games. Sebastian Cole leads the scoring charts for the Limerick side, while Tiras Morton leads the league in assists, rebounds, and steals. Tony Hehir's men recently dismantled Tralee 88-69 in a league contest, taking a commanding 14-point halftime lead before sealing a 19-point victory on the road.

Meanwhile, Limerick Eagles are away to holders Killester in the Men’s National Cup this Saturday with a 6pm tip-off. The Eagles enter the fixture as MD1 National Cup champions after defeating Drogheda Wolves 83-67 in the final, where Ryan Leonard top-scored. Key performers Alex Carlisle, Darragh Horkan, and Tobias Christensen have carried their strong form from last season into the current Domino’s Men’s Super League campaign.

In the Women’s Cup, Celtics welcome Cavan Eagles to Crescent College on Saturday evening at 7.45pm. Jeni Levine heads the scoring charts for the Limerick side with 146 points so far, while also leading the league in assists.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362925.localAngle: Limerick basketball sides Celtics and Eagles face high-stakes National Cup fixtures this weekend across both men's and women's competitions.

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53564.headline: Limerick GAA launch 2027 O'Neills jersey featuring Treaty Stone and historic green shades
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53564.summary: Limerick GAA has unveiled its new O'Neills kit for the 2027 season, combining a familiar green design with historic nods to the county's kits from the 2000s and 2010s. The new strip went on sale on Friday, November 6.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53564.story:
Limerick GAA supporters can now purchase the county's new strip for the 2027 season following its official release in conjunction with O'Neills.

The design follows a growing trend across various sports of taking elements from historical kits and giving them a modern twist. The jersey retains a mostly familiar green shirt paired with white shorts and socks, but incorporates a darker shade of green along the sleeves and shoulders to contrast with the brighter body. This darker tone recalls Limerick strips from the 2000s and 2010s.

Local heritage is also woven directly into the sportswear. The sleeves and both sides of the shorts feature a distinct depiction of the Treaty Stone. Continuing a practice in place since 2019, the front of the shirt remains free of any corporate sponsor. O'Neills' signature three stripes run partially up the shirt from the bottom to meet the stripes on the shorts.

The new kit officially went on sale on Friday, November 6, and is available to purchase at Gleeson's Sport Scene and through the O'Neills online store.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53564.localAngle: The new kit features depictions of Limerick's iconic Treaty Stone and will be worn by county teams throughout the 2027 season.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53564.originalTitle: Limerick GAA honour the past in 2027 kit release

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53575.headline: Limerick Celtics Claim Top Spot in Domino’s Men’s Super League
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53575.summary: Limerick Celtics lead the Domino’s Men’s Super League with five wins from six games, following an 88-69 victory over Garvey’s Tralee Warriors.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53575.story:
Limerick Celtics have climbed to the summit of the Domino’s Men’s Super League after securing five wins from their opening six games. Head coach Tony Hehir’s side cemented their position on October 30 with an 88-69 victory over Garvey’s Tralee Warriors at the UL Arena, led by 21 points from Philip Kearney.

Hehir attributes the team's strong start to a combination of home-grown talent and key professional signings, including Sebastian Cole, Peter Turay, and Tiras Morton. The squad has also been bolstered by the addition of underage players Callum Keys, Hubert Gocek, and Max Turski.

The rise of Limerick basketball is further highlighted by the competitive performances of the Limerick Eagles, fostering a local rivalry that recently drew a substantial crowd to the UL Arena. Celtics will look to defend their league-leading position when they face UCC Demons in Round Seven on November 14.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53575.localAngle: The Celtics' success and the emerging derby rivalry with Limerick Eagles are drawing strong local crowds and boosting the profile of indoor sport in the city.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53575.originalTitle: ‘Limerick basketball on the rise’ as Celtics take top spot in Super League

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362891.headline: Shannon Airport Group shortlisted for Public Enterprise of the Year
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362891.summary: The Shannon Airport Group has been named a finalist for Public Enterprise of the Year at the 2026 Business & Finance Awards. The winners will be announced at a gala ceremony in Dublin on December 10.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362891.story:
The Shannon Airport Group has secured a shortlist nomination for Public Enterprise of the Year at the upcoming 2026 Business & Finance Awards. This marks the second consecutive year the group has reached the final stage in the category.

In the running for the top prize, The Shannon Airport Group is joined by fellow nominees An Post, Fáilte Ireland, and Údarás na Gaeltachta. The category recognises excellence in operations, stakeholder engagement, and the delivery of sustainable public value.

Ray O’Driscoll, CEO of The Shannon Airport Group, welcomed the announcement, noting that the recognition reflects recent progress in passenger growth, facility investment, and sustainability. "As Shannon Airport and the Shannon Airport Business Park continue to grow, we’re proud of the role we play in supporting tourism, investment and job creation across the West of Ireland," he said.

The overall winners of the 52nd annual Business & Finance Awards will be revealed during a gala ceremony at the Convention Centre in Dublin on Thursday, December 10.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362891.localAngle: The Shannon Airport Group plays a vital role in supporting tourism, investment, and job creation across Limerick and the wider Mid-West region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362891.originalTitle: Airport on runway for Public Enterprise Awards

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53598.headline: O’Donovan Seeks Council Answers After Adare Feral Cat Habitat Paved Over
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53598.summary: Limerick City and County Council has paved over a wooded area in Adare used by a feral cat colony to install a rainwater system. While shelters remain accessible, Councillor Elisa O’Donovan is calling for assurances regarding the cats' welfare and ecological impact assessments.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53598.story:
A wooded area in Adare that served as a long-standing home for a colony of feral cats has been paved over, prompting calls for clarification from local representatives. The council-owned site was altered to accommodate a rainwater-harvesting system installed by Adare Tidy Towns, alongside the replacement of surrounding fencing for health and safety reasons.

Councillor Elisa O’Donovan raised the issue with Limerick City and County Council after learning of the works. While the local authority has confirmed that the cats' shelters remain in place and that the new fencing allows continued access for both the animals and the volunteers who feed them, Cllr O’Donovan argues that the broader environmental impact requires scrutiny.

Speaking to the Limerick Voice, Cllr O’Donovan said she is seeking assurances regarding the suitability of the current shelters and whether any ecological assessments were conducted before the project began. She emphasized that even small green spaces function as vital local habitats that demand careful planning.

The councillor has urged the local authority to consult directly with the volunteers who have cared for the Adare colony over the years, ensuring the animals retain secure living conditions and that greenery is restored where possible. She noted that supporting community volunteers and protecting vulnerable local wildlife are important responsibilities for the local community.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53598.localAngle: The issue involves council-owned land and local animal welfare volunteers in the County Limerick town of Adare.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53598.originalTitle: Concern over welfare of Limerick cats after habitat is paved over

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362939.headline: Tributes Paid Following Passing of Garryowen Stalwart John Fahey
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362939.summary: Garryowen Football Club has paid warm tributes following the death of former President, Chairman, and Trustee John Fahey. Fahey, a familiar face around the club, presided over the historic 2006/07 season when the club achieved a unique clean sweep of four major trophies.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362939.story:
Garryowen Football Club is mourning the loss of John Fahey, a prominent club stalwart who served as President, Chairman, and Trustee. Tributes have poured in from across the local rugby community following his passing.

Honorary Secretary Sandra Maher remembered Fahey for his immense contribution to the club and Irish rugby. She noted that as recently as the previous Saturday, he had been supporting the senior team, enjoying a pre-match meal with friend Steve McDonagh, and looking forward to an upcoming trip to Armagh. 

"We will miss his gentle manner, his kindness, his friendship and the genuine interest he took in everyone around him," Ms Maher said in a statement. She added that he was reunited in death with his dearest wife, Kathleen.

Recalling his leadership, past President Billy Purcell noted on rip.ie that during Fahey’s tenure as Chairman in the 2006/07 season, Garryowen accomplished a nationwide unique feat by winning the Grand Slam, All-Ireland League, All-Ireland Cup, Munster Senior Cup, and Munster Junior Cup. Outside of his deep involvement in local rugby, Fahey was widely known in Limerick for his many years working as General Manager at the Limerick Inn.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362939.localAngle: John Fahey was a deeply embedded figure in Limerick rugby and hospitality, having served as General Manager of the Limerick Inn and leader of Garryowen FC.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362939.originalTitle: Tributes after passing of Garryowen stalwart

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53587.headline: Folk Band Kingfishr Surprise Limerick Fans with Pop-Up Gig on Cruises Street
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53587.summary: Limerick shoppers got a surprise treat when folk trio Kingfishr performed an impromptu gig on Cruises Street as part of a four-city whistle-stop tour to announce their upcoming second album.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53587.story:
Shoppers on Cruises Street were treated to an unexpected performance on Saturday afternoon as folk band Kingfishr arrived in the city for a surprise pop-up gig.

The trio—made up of Eddie Keogh, Eoghan McGrath and Eoin Fitzgibbon—took to the Limerick street at approximately 1.30pm as part of a whirlwind tour across four Irish cities in one day. The band kicked off their schedule in Galway at 10.30am before heading to the Treaty City, with subsequent stops planned for Cork at 5pm and Dublin at 9.30pm.

The surprise visit was organised to celebrate the announcement of their second album, 'Weight of the Feather', which is scheduled for release on April 9, 2027. The album's title track will be released next Friday, November 13.

The appearance carried a strong local resonance for the band, who are former University of Limerick students. The visit comes ahead of two major homecoming concerts at Thomond Park scheduled for July 2027, following a string of successes that includes their breakthrough hit 'Killeagh' and their debut album, 'Halcyon'.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53587.localAngle: The band have strong ties to Limerick as former University of Limerick students and are returning to the city for major concerts at Thomond Park in July 2027.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53587.originalTitle: Kingfishr take over Cruises Street today for surprise pop-up

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362898.headline: TUS President Vincent Cunnane oversees final graduation before January retirement
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362898.summary: Founding TUS President Professor Vincent Cunnane conferred his final student in Limerick on Friday, bringing an estimated 35,000 graduates to his total over his career.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362898.story:
Technological University of the Shannon (TUS) founding President Professor Vincent Cunnane presided over his final conferring ceremony in Limerick on Friday, marking the end of a tenure that has seen him personally confer an estimated 35,000 graduates across three higher education institutions.

Fittingly for an academic who began his career in scientific research, the final student to cross the stage was James Ryan from Mungret, Limerick. Ryan was awarded a Doctor of Philosophy for his research into how advanced technology can make workplaces safer. Professor Cunnane, who will retire at the end of January, admitted he felt emotional during the ceremony and said graduation events had been among the most rewarding parts of his presidency.

"Graduations are where it all comes together, where all those stories culminate in success. They walk across the stage as equals, as professionals, as people with a future," Professor Cunnane said. "And for me, that's just the magic of being in this role. And I'm going to miss it terribly."

In his final address, he told the Class of 2026 that human judgement and critical thinking would become increasingly valuable in a world shaped by Artificial Intelligence. Professor Cunnane will be succeeded by Professor Paul Connolly, who takes up the role in spring 2027.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362898.localAngle: The final graduation ceremony took place in Limerick, concluding with a local PhD recipient from Mungret.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362896.headline: Major Irish Banks Launch Professional Banking Apprenticeship Offering NFQ Level 8 Degree
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362896.summary: AIB, Bank of Ireland, and PTSB have partnered with the IOB to launch a new banking apprenticeship. The programme gives 75 participants paid experience alongside studying for a Level 8 degree.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362896.story:
A new professional banking apprenticeship has been launched by the IOB in a major partnership involving AIB, Bank of Ireland, and PTSB. The initiative offers participants the opportunity to earn an NFQ Level 8 degree while gaining paid, practical experience within the banking sector.

Apprentices will split their time between working in the industry and studying with the IOB, which is a recognised college of UCD. The scheme is open to school leavers and anyone looking for a career change, provided applicants are at least 18 years old on or before August 31, 2027.

A total of 75 places will be made available for the first intake of students. Applications are now open, with the successful candidates set to commence the programme in October 2027. Further details and application information can be found at apprenticeship.ie or via the IOB website.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362896.localAngle: The nationwide apprenticeship programme provides training and employment pathways for prospective banking professionals in Limerick and across the country.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362896.originalTitle: New apprenticeship programme for Limerick bankers

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362904.headline: Council to assess feasibility of new Castleconnell to Nelsons Cross walkway
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362904.summary: Independent Councillor Ursula Gavan has called for a new pedestrian route connecting Castleconnell Campsite to the village via Nelsons Cross. The local authority has agreed to carry out a preliminary assessment of the route.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362904.story:
Limerick City and County Council has agreed to examine the feasibility of building a new walkway linking the Castleconnell Campsite to the village via Nelsons Cross.

The project was pushed forward by Independent Councillor Ursula Gavan during this month's Metropolitan District meeting, where she urged the local authority to prioritise the infrastructure.

Responding to the proposal, council officials noted that the route could significantly improve pedestrian connectivity and encourage greater access between the campsite and local amenities.

The Council's Transportation, Mobility & Public Realm Directorate confirmed that the local Area Office will now conduct a preliminary assessment. This initial phase will look at the feasibility of the route, required land, and estimated construction costs before potential funding streams are explored.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362904.localAngle: The proposed walkway aims to improve pedestrian access and local amenities for residents and visitors in Castleconnell.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362904.originalTitle: Cllr Gavan calls for walkway from Castleconnell to Nelsons Cross

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362901.headline: Banned 1971 Masterpiece 'The Devils' Finally Sees Irish Release After 50 Years
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362901.summary: Ken Russell's controversial 1971 film 'The Devils' is finally screening in Ireland in a landmark director's cut. The film was banned for over half a century due to its depictions of religious persecution and institutional corruption.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362901.story:
Cinema history's most notorious and controversial film, Ken Russell’s 1971 masterpiece 'The Devils', is finally seeing the light of day in Ireland after being banned for over half a century. The film has returned in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of the original vision.

Inspired by the true story of 17th-century priest Urbain Grandier, played by Oliver Reed, the film explores his accusation of bewitching a convent of nuns. Grandier's unorthodox views on sex and religion draw a passionate following, including the sexually obsessed Sister Jeanne, played by Vanessa Redgrave. To gain control of France, power-hungry Cardinal Richelieu, played by Christopher Logue, works to eliminate Grandier by portraying him as a satanist and sparking public outrage.

Upon its release over 50 years ago, the work was condemned as sacrilegious and reprehensible, sparking scandal over its depiction of institutional religion and possessed nuns. The explosive fever dream features surrealistic sexual defilement, manic spiritual elation, and medieval violence and torture.

While the film might not stir the same level of outrage by today’s standards, its core message concerning the collusion of church and state, religious persecution, and institutional corruption continues to strike a chord with modern audiences.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362901.localAngle: Film enthusiasts across Limerick can now view the landmark director's cut of Ken Russell's notorious 1971 work following its long-awaited Irish release.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362906.headline: Over €150,000 Allocated for Youth Facilities and Equipment Across Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362906.summary: More than €150,000 in funding has been secured for youth facilities and equipment across Limerick, supporting projects from Rathkeale to the city. The investment will fund minor works, digital equipment, and safety upgrades.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362906.story:
More than €150,000 in funding has been secured for youth facilities and equipment across Limerick, following an announcement made last month by Minister Patrick O'Donovan.

The funding package includes €8,530 for Limerick Youth Service’s Rathkeale/Askeaton project and a combined €24,739 for the two Foróige Loobagh projects. Additional allocations will go to Limerick Sports Partnership, Limerick Youth Theatre, Bluebox Creative Learning, and various youth services operating across Limerick city.

The investment is earmarked to support a range of improvements, including minor building works, digital equipment, recreation resources, arts and music equipment, accessibility improvements, and safety upgrades.

“This is a practical investment in our young people,” Minister O’Donovan said. “It will help youth services across Limerick replace ageing equipment, improve their buildings and provide welcoming spaces.”
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362906.localAngle: The funding directly benefits youth clubs, organizations, and services across Limerick city and county, including Rathkeale, Askeaton, and the Loobagh projects.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362906.originalTitle: Over €150,000 announced in youth facilities and equipment in Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362937.headline: Contracts Signed for €28M Limerick Level Crossing Overhauls
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362937.summary: Iarnród Éireann has signed a €28 million contract to upgrade seven public road level crossings, including the closure of crossings at Fantstown and Thomastown in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362937.story:
Contracts have officially been signed for a major €28 million improvement project affecting seven manned public road level crossings, including key locations in County Limerick. 

Under the works funded by the Department of Transport through the National Transport Authority, the level crossings at Fantstown and Thomastown will be permanently closed. In their place, new replacement bridges or alternative road solutions will be provided at both Limerick locations.

Following a recent procurement and tendering process, contractor Jons Civil Engineering Ltd is expected to arrive on site in the coming days to begin the infrastructure upgrades. 

Irish rail authorities have confirmed that the extensive improvement project is scheduled for completion by April 2028.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362937.localAngle: The project directly impacts local transport infrastructure in Limerick with the permanent closure and replacement of level crossings at Fantstown and Thomastown.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362937.originalTitle: Contracts signed for road levels crossings in Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362945.headline: Two Arrested in Enniskillen Over Murder of Limerick Mother Carrie Mullane
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362945.summary: Two more people have been arrested by the PSNI on suspicion of the murder of 39-year-old Limerick mother-of-four Carrie Mullane, whose remains are currently being searched for in County Fermanagh. A man has already appeared in court charged in connection with her disappearance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362945.story:
Two additional people have been arrested in connection with the ongoing murder investigation into Limerick woman Carrie Mullane. A woman in her 60s and a man in his 30s were taken into custody in Enniskillen as part of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) probe.

Ms Mullane, a 39-year-old mother of four, was last seen on October 10 after travelling to County Fermanagh. The PSNI believe she was killed shortly after arriving in the area. Authorities are actively searching for her remains, with police divers focusing efforts on a section of Upper Lough Erne near Enniskillen over the weekend.

A 35-year-old man was arrested last week in connection with the case and has already appeared in court charged with murder and preventing the lawful burial of a corpse.

Detectives are continuing to appeal for public assistance. The PSNI has asked anyone with information, or who may have captured CCTV, phone, or dash-cam footage that could aid the investigation, to come forward.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362945.localAngle: The victim is a 39-year-old mother of four from Limerick who travelled to County Fermanagh before her disappearance.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362945.originalTitle: Two further arrests in Limerick mother of four murder probe

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362914.headline: New residents group backs six-week traffic closure of The Crescent for Christmas
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362914.summary: A newly formed residents group supports closing The Crescent on O'Connell Avenue to traffic for six weeks this Christmas for a festive fayre. However, local traders warn the closure could cause severe traffic congestion and harm Christmas trade.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362914.story:
A newly formed Limerick residents group has thrown its weight behind proposals to close The Crescent on O'Connell Avenue to traffic for six weeks this Christmas. The Limerick City Centre Residents’ Voice (LCCRV), which was formed a month ago and recently hosted Mayor John Moran at a meeting, described the festive plans for Christmas 2026 as "ambitious". The proposed Christmas Fayre would span The Crescent, O'Connell Avenue, and Arthur’s Quay Park.

In a statement, LCCRV argued that vibrant public events help support economic activity and strengthen community spirit in the city. "As people who live, work and raise families in this area, we look forward to experiencing the buzz, atmosphere and sense of occasion that these events can bring," the group said, comparing the prospect to historic festive celebrations in cities like Prague and London.

However, the plans have met resistance from local business owners concerned about traffic disruption during the busiest retail period of the year. Fifth-generation city shop owner Shane Gleeson urged the local authority to vary the event licence and relocate the Christmas Market to Arthur’s Quay or Honan’s Quay.

Mr Gleeson warned that holding the event at The Crescent would lead to severe traffic congestion and negatively impact trade when maximum traffic flow is vital for businesses. He added that relocating the fayre to Honan's Quay would better complement the existing ice rink and offer easier access to nearby parking facilities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362914.localAngle: The proposed traffic closure of The Crescent and the staging of a major Christmas Fayre directly impacts city centre residents, motorists, and local traders in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362914.originalTitle: Newly formed group welcomes closure of Crescent despite traders concerns

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362910.headline: Shannon Man Charged with Race Hate Crime and Threating Security at UHL
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362910.summary: A 38-year-old man has appeared in court charged with a racially motivated hate crime and breaching the peace at University Hospital Limerick on Halloween night. The judge granted bail with conditions after hearing the accused is seeking help for drug addiction.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362910.story:
A man appeared before Ennis District Court on Monday charged in connection with an alleged race hate crime committed against a Pakistani security guard at University Hospital Limerick (UHL) on Halloween night. 

At the court hearing, Garda Roisín Moran stated that Martin O’Callaghan (38), of High Street, Lissycasey, tried to flee Garda custody at the hospital's A&E Department on Saturday, October 31st. Garda Moran alleged that Mr O’Callaghan called a security staff member, who is a Pakistani national, 'monkey face' in the presence of Gardaí, made a sound of pooling saliva as if to spit, and claimed he was HIV positive.

Gardaí had arrested Mr O’Callaghan earlier that day in Kilrush over a separate public order incident. He was brought to UHL after telling officers he had swallowed a bag of cocaine, though he ultimately refused medical assistance at the hospital. He is formally charged with provoking a breach of the peace and demonstrating hatred towards the security guard on account of his race, colour, or nationality.

Defence counsel Elaine Davern Wiseman BL told the court that her client's wish is to get help for a long-standing drug abuse struggle. Judge Catherine Ryan granted bail, noting the allegations are of particular concern given they occurred in a hospital setting. Mr O’Callaghan was remanded on bail to appear again in Ennis District Court on November 25, under conditions that include staying out of Kilrush and residing at a bail address in Rossbracken, Shannon.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362910.localAngle: The alleged incident took place at University Hospital Limerick, a vital regional healthcare facility serving the local community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362910.originalTitle: Court appearance on charge of ‘monkey face’ taunt at security guard

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362942.headline: Pedestrian killed in single-car collision on M20 northbound outside Limerick City
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362942.summary: A pedestrian was struck and killed by a car on the M20 motorway between Raheen and Dooradoyle on Sunday evening. Gardaí have launched an investigation and are appealing for witnesses and dash-cam footage.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362942.story:
Gardaí are investigating a fatal traffic incident after a pedestrian was killed in a single-car collision on the M20 motorway outside Limerick City on Sunday evening (November 8).

The incident occurred at approximately 5.20pm on the northbound stretch of the motorway between Junction 3 (Raheen) and Junction 2 (Dooradoyle). The pedestrian was pronounced dead at the scene, and no other injuries were reported.

The M20 was temporarily closed following the collision to allow Garda Forensic Collision Investigators to conduct a technical examination. The local coroner has been notified, and arrangements are being made for a post-mortem examination.

Authorities are urging anyone who was travelling on the M20 between Junctions 3 and 2 on Sunday evening from 5pm to 5.30pm, particularly those with dash-cam or other camera footage, to contact Henry Street Garda Station on 061 212 400 or the Garda Confidential Line on 1800 666 111.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362942.localAngle: The fatal collision occurred on a major commuter route just outside Limerick City, prompting a local appeal for witnesses by Henry Street Gardaí.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362942.originalTitle: Pedestrian killed in crash on motorway outside Limerick City
